text: The elections to the 15" Lok Sabha are taking place at a time when the entire world is in a state of flux. The global economy has virtually come to a grinding halt. Simultaneously, wanton terrorism and mindless acts of counter-terrorism have claimed thousands of innocent lives. World leaders, Economists and Policy-framers are frantically searching for solutions to these challenges confronting mankind.

In this global scenario, wrong policies, spineless governance, visionless leadership and tardy programme implementation turned out to be the hallmark of the UPA Government in India. The growth bubble of the past few years has burst. Manufacturing is now recording negative growth. The services sector too has suffered collateral damage. Millions have lost their jobs. Suicides by farmers continue unabated. The stock market collapsed. Inflation, notwithstanding the recent proclamations of the Government, has not yet abated, as witnessed by the continued high prices of primary commodities and food items.

Terrorists can strike virtually at any time and anywhere, making every: place in India totally unsafe. The Police Force in this country has not been keeping pace with these developments, both in terms of intelligence inputs and in terms of technology. Further, India faces hostile neighbours across all her borders. Yet, the Defence Forces are not in any state of preparedness with the UPA Government having significantly compromised on the Nation’s security. Illegal immigrants continue to gnaw at the vitals of our economy, while there is a concerted effort by terrorists to hit at the national economy too.

The curse on the Nation for the past five years, viz the UPA Government, has virtually allowed all these problems to grow in the shores of India by its irresponsible policies. Instead of foreseeing, planning and then insulating the Nation from the ill effects of globalisation as suggested by many leaders, thinkers and analysts, the UPA Government continued its dogmatic approach to reckless globalisation.

The consequence of all this is that rather late in the day, India seeks to insulate, disengage and decouple from the global economy so as to escape the ill effects of globalisation. In the process the common man has suffered heavily.

The net effect is that while the Indian economy was reportedly recording robust growth according to statistics put out by the Government, farmers were committing suicide. While India boasted of healthy foreign exchange reserves, exports were falling. Employment opportunities were dwindling. Huge sums of money were apparently spent on the Social Sector by the UPA Government. Yet, India languishes at the bottom of the Human Development Index at the global level. It is indeed a reflection of the paradoxical state of affairs in the country that while India boasts of some of the world’s richest people, some of the districts of the country are comparable to sub-Saharan Africa - one of the poorest and most underdeveloped regions of the world.
In short, the UPA has been long on words and short on performance. ;

The people of Tami! Nadu have had to face a double whammy after the DMK - one of the important constituents of the UPA Government at the Centre - formed a minority Government in 2006. With its reckless poll promises, the minority DMK Government has virtually ruined the fiscal position of the State, assiduously built under the previous AIADMK regime. It has marred the industrial climate of the State to such an extent, through frequent power cuts, poor infrastructure and of course

corrupt governance, that Tamil Nadu - the numero uno, the pride of India till 2006, is now no longer the preferred destination for both domestic and international investments. Deteriorating law and order, unrest in the legal profession, an aggressive ruling-party-backed sand-smuggling mafia, campuses that have turned into slaughter houses and politically inspired mayhem by the law-enforcing agencies have all only accentuated the already deteriorating situation.
Again, it is a strange paradox that in this depressing scenario, only one particular family - that of Mr Karunanidhi, the Chief Minister of the minority DMK Government -- continues to prosper.

Some of the State’s prominent industrial clusters in Tamil Nadu are facing imminent closure. Agriculture is in dire straits, especially in the Cauvery delta region, thanks to the inept handling of the Cauvery river water dispute with Karnataka by the minority DMK Government. The Sri Lankan imbroglio is continuing to take its toll of the fishing communities of the State. Law and order is virtually non-existent with even Courts not functioning for months together in the State. Yet, Mr Karunanidhi lives in his own make-believe world, spending time to broker peace amongst the innumerable warring members of his huge family who control various family businesses.
Never in the history of Independent India have we witnessed such complete disconnect between the elected representatives and the electorate, both at the Central as well as the State levels.

This supine indifference to overall governance by the UPA Government and its inability to take appropriate steps to tackle critical situations has greatly damaged the social and capital base of the country.

The UPA Government by its consistent acts of dividing people on the basis of caste and community, so as to prolong its tenure, has left a fragmented society with several fault lines. The entire country is a tinderbox — ready to explode at the slightest provocation.

Yet, India continues to remain intact and out-perform many economies at the global level. And for this the credit must go to the average Indian -- farmers, teachers, salaried employees, artisans, labourers, workers, government employees, self-employed, students, senior citizens, community leaders and of course the lady of the house.

The AIADMK salutes the Common Man / Woman of India, for his / her perseverance and tenacity in fighting all odds for the past five years. The AIADMK places this manifesto for the forthcoming elections before the people, with a view to leveraging the performance of the ordinary Indian to extraordinary levels.

The AIADMK takes this opportunity to pledge its complete support to all sections of the population who have been victims of the gross neglect and mis-governance of the UPA Government. The AIADMK assures them that the worst is over and the time for redemption is NOW.

The AIADMK also seeks the good wishes and support of all sections of the people in the forthcoming Parliamentary Elections in order to have the required strength for the onerous task of building a better India.

Tough times call for tough decisions. And tough decisions can be taken only by mentally tough people. What India needs today is a stable Government headed by a strong Prime Minister, who is not only capable of identifying India's specific problems but who is also a leader with a vision who can ensure proper implementation of. plans, programmes and policies. India needs a dynamic team that is capable of out-of-the-box thinking and an effective action plan.

The global imperative of the need for a strong Indian leader is equally compelling. Given the emergence of a multi-polar world, India needs to be appropriately represented at the global level. The AIADMK believes that it is India that can lead the world out of the present impasse — both politically and economically. The AIADMK foresees that India has a definite role in the emerging global order.
It is the proud privilege of the AIADMK party to be guided by Ms Jayalalithaa in the forthcoming general elections. It is widely known

that Ms Jayalalithaa - Amma, as she is fondly referred to by her party men - is a multifaceted personality who has dominated the State’s politics for well over two decades - for over 27 years, to be precise. Known for her administrative acumen, she has been the Chief Minister of the State of Tamil Nadu on two occasions - from 1991 to 1996 and again from 2001 to 2006, besides being a member of the Rajya Sabha for a term from 1984.

For her age, Ms Jayalalithaa is perhaps the only Indian politician who has had two successful stints as the Chief Minister of a large Indian state besides being the leader of the opposition for two terms of the State Assembly. Over the past two decades, she has guided the destiny of the State in various capacities, so much so that today she is one of the most towering personalities in the Indian political landscape.
Naturally the aspirations of the people of the State are obvious.

Ms Jayalalithaa, with her vast administrative experience, political acumen, understanding of India, extraordinary vision and of course sagacious leadership is expected to play a dominant role in guiding the destiny of the country in the immediate future. The AIADMK is fully confident of the fact that every vote cast in favour of the AIADMK-led alliance by the people of Tamil Nadu is a vote for a leader from the State to play a pro-active, dominant and decisive role in the formation of the next Government at the Centre.

It is in this connection that it will be the endeavour of the AIADMK led by Puratchi Thalaivi J Jayalalithaa, to coordinate and cooperate with like-minded forces at the national level to ensure that the aspirations of the State and Nation are fully met.

Against formidable odds, Perarignar Anna had started and built the DMK Party and in course of time transformed it into an organisatign akin to a closely knit affectionate political family. He never aspired for any personal wealth or political power for himself or for his family members. | He treated all Tamilians as his kin and utilised every opportunity to ensure political, economic and social development of the Tamil race and

the people of Tamil Nadu. Even when he formed the DMK, following differences with his mentor Periyar, he retained enough respect for, Periyar as to reserve for him the post of President of the party. He,° himself, preferred to be the General Secretary of the DMK.

Karunanidhi, who succeeded him, on the other hand, anointed himself as party President, throwing to the winds the high norms set by Anna. Perarignar Anna transformed the DMK party into a family. In direct contrast, Karunanidhi converted his family into the Party.

The AIADMK is a party founded by Puratchi Thalaivar MGR based on the ideals laid out by his mentor, Perarignar Anna. From its foundation on the 17th October 1972, the AIADMK has a glorious history. Under the leadership of Puratchi Thalaivar MGR, the same pattern of-organisational structure was followed as that propounded by Perarignar Anna. Under him, the Party had very many achievements to its credit with the massive support and affectionate attachment of the people.

The ideals of these two visionary leaders have been the guiding beacons for Puratchi Thalaivi Jayalalithaa, who has emerged not only as a charismatic mass leader but also as an iron-willed person who can provide the AIADMK party, the State of Tamil Nadu and the Indian Nation with the in-depth guidance and leadership of character that are necessary at this stage.
Given this ‘background, the AIADMK has pleasure in placing before the people “An Agenda For A Better India” in the form of its Election Manifesto for the Lok Sabha Elections, 2009.
The AIADMK, through this Manifesto, pledges to provide transparent, responsive, honest, secular and sensitive governance to the people of India.

The UPA Government has completely messed up the Nation’s finances. Today the fiscal situation is alarming. With fiscal deficit estimated to be in excess of 10% for 2008-09 and still higher for 2009- 10, the mess created by the UPA Government would take several years to be neutralised.

The AIADMK shall work to bring out a white paper on the finances of the Central Government similar to the one brought out by the Tamil Nadu Government in 2001 under the leadership of Ms Jayalalithaa. While fiscal discipline needs to be maintained, the AIADMK is fully conscious of the fact that these are not times for fiscal orthodoxy. The AIADMK will bring back fiscal discipline in the finances of the Central Government, while the FRBM (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) targets will be reworked, in the face of the global downturn.

Keeping these objectives uppermost in mind, the AIADMK proposes the following changes on the economic front: e Ensure that more money is available in the hands of the people. e All salaried employees to be exempted from Income Tax. e« Income tax exemption limit for all others to be increased to Rs 5 Lakhs per annum. e Repeal Fringe Benefit Tax and Banking Cash Transaction Tax. e FDI in retail, real estate and higher education will not be allowed. Present limits on FDI in insurance sector to continue. e No SEZs on cultivable farmlands. e Market-rate compensation, employment preferénce and shares in SEZ holdings for those selling lands to SEZ.

The AIADMK shall: e Stabilise the precipitous fall in the value of the Rupee and accept the recommendations of the Tarapore Committee on control of gyrations of the Rupee vis-a-vis major currencies of the world. The idea of Capital account convertibility to be given up. e Address the gyrations in the domestic markets caused by the sudden surge in forex inflows and outflows through appropriate
policy interventions. FDI policy has to be in tune with the overall economic policies and cannot be rooted to neo-liberal dogmas.

Know Your Customer (KYC) norms for foreign investment to be made ona par with that of Indian investors. e War on wasteful expenditure of Government. e Develop modern satellite administrative townships for our metros - facilities in these townships to be on a par with other Asian countries with a view to decongesting cities. e Public sector banks to be sufficiently capitalised. The Raghuram Rajan report on financial sector liberalisation shall be referred to a committee, and contentious issues as well as developments in the world of finance shall be factored before implementation. e Big integrated plan for infrastructure with thrust on modernisation of railways including the introduction of new freight corridors, improvement of water bodies, irrigation, North-South and East-West road corridors, power and of course ports. e Modernisation of existing major and minor airports to be expedited.

North-East to have a new modern airport to facilitate tourism. e Ensure a Golden Quadrilateral as well as North-South and East-West corridors for upgrading the Indian Railways to international levels. The AIADMK shall usher in Bullet Trains linking all important metros that would travel at international speeds, backed up with international safety norms and comforts. e Institutionalising adequate credit flows to both Agriculture and Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) sectors. e Evolve consensus on the on-going Doha Round Negotiations within the WTO agenda. Ensure we roll back any autonomous policy liberalization. If necessary, negotiate from a clean slate rather than from a position of weakness. e Not to allow foreign law firms as well as accounting firms to function in India ahead of General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS) negotiations within the WTO regime. These sectors will be

liberalised only after prior consultation with the Bar Council of India and the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. e Coordinate with various Governments and multilateral agencies on the issue of tackling the global financial crisis and providing appropriate leadership to the global economy. e Elimination of power shortages in the next 5 years. Major thrust for all wind, solar and other non-conventional power projects. e Review of coal, oil & gas as well as well as telecom policy of the ; Central Government. The controversial Spectrum allocations made by the UPA regime will be reviewed and the allocation will be made again to ensure that the revenue due to the Indian Government is realized in full. e Bring about a new energy policy for the country that would include hydro carbons and coal, as well as other conventional and non-conventional sources of energy - seek to improve power generation by 1,00,000 MW in the next five years. The Transmission & Distribution (T&D) losses in India are far above the international norm while the Plant Load Factor (PLF) of some of our power plants is far below economic levels of operations. The AIADMK shall ensure a reduction of T&D losses while improving the PLF. The AIADMK shall repose confidence in our scientists in harnessing safe and sufficient Nuclear Technology for the country by exploiting the abundant natural resources available in India. e Revive the Indo-Iran oil pipeline, if necessary routing it through the sea. e Review the role of the Planning Commission and ensure that it is made into an advisory body on all economic issues faced by the Government. e Come down heavily on Banks charging usurious rates of ‘interest from credit card holders. e No privatisation of pension funds and not allowing their entry into the stock market.

A major issue that is eating into the vitals of the Indian Society as well as its economy is corruption. Corruption in the Government stems from poor governance, lack of accountability and bad legislations. e The AIADMK shall address these issues both at macro and micro levels by reviewing unwanted legislations, toning up governance and by strengthening grassroots democracy. e Immediate action to bring back Indian money (estimated at anywhere between Rs 7.5 lakh crores to Rs 75 lakh crores) lying unproductively in International tax havens. e Review the practice of issuing Participatory Notes, which was substantially responsible for the melt-down of the Indian economy. e Review all treaties facilitating money laundering. e Issue of fake currency to be tackled on a war-footing. e No more divesting of shares of sensitive or profit-making PSUs and nationalized banks. e Total independence for all market regulators like SEBI, RBI, PFRDA (Provident Fund Regulation & Development Authority), IRDA (Insurance Regulation & Development Authority) and TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India). e Review specific Double Taxation Avoidance Treaties, especially the one with Mauritius, based on the observations of the Supreme Court in the Azadi Bachao Andolan case. e Come down heavily on tax evaders, black marketeers, hoarders and speculators e The AIADMK also- shall come down _ heavily on_ those Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), especially those funded from abroad, which under the garb of doing service for our poor are carrying out anti-national activities.

e The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), in his reports, has squarely blamed the UPA Government for tardy programme implementation. The report has stated that the UPA Government had met expenditure targets for several schemes by simply transferring sums aggregating to Rs. 51,259.85 crores for 2007-08 to the accounts of several NGOs, autonomous bodies and societies. The CAG admitted that he was unable to verify the same. The AIADMK shall investigate this matter and take it to a logical conclusion. e The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) is now without any legal teeth and proper infrastructure to investigate sophisticated frauds. The AIADMK shall ensure that it gets both.

The AIADMK realises that the present UPA dispensation was one of the most corrupt regimes ever to occupy office in India. There are allegations of corruption against most cabinet ministers in the UPA Government, the most notable one being the scandal in allocating Spectrum for mobile telephone operations.

The Union Minister for Communications is charged with having adopted wrong procedures to hand over 2-G Spectrum licences to unknown players for a song. The loss to the Nation due to this scam is reportedly well over Rs. 1,00,000 Crores. This sort of consideration has obviously been given to the beneficiaries only on receipt of substantial amounts of money as illegal gratification. The AIADMK will institute an inquiry into this multi-crore scam and ensure that the perpetrators are brought to book.
India, for the past decade or so, has been witnessing jobless growth.

What is more alarming is the fact that, according to some estimates in the past few years, more than 55 million people have been pushed below the poverty line. Employment generation, both by the Government and in the private sector, poses a serious challenge to future Governments. By providing an impetus to both Industry and Agriculture, the AIADMK is certain that considerable job opportunities will be opened up in the private sector, which will more than adequately compensate for the loss of jobs caused by. the present recession. The AIADMK is confident that

increased social sector and infrastructure spending, in the next few years, will provide a new impetus for employment generation. Secondly, by reducing taxes, the AIADMK seeks to leverage the multiplier effect as more spending would lead to more consumption, which would spur demand and thereby job opportunities.

Plans: e Filling up of 6 lakh existing vacancies in Defence and Central services. e 5 lakh casual workers in Central Services to be regularised. e 3 lakh Extra Departmental workers in Postal Services to be regularised. e 100 million jobs to be provided in the next five years.

For three successive decades beginning from 1980, India has been witnessing a robust growth in excess of six percent. Nevertheless, India continues to languish at the bottom of the Human Development Index (HDI) at the international level. The ignominy is best captured by the fact that India is ranked 132 amongst about 180 countries, while several of our war-torn, tiny neighbours are ranked above us. Once again, this piece of statistics cruelly exposes the claim of the UPA Government about its concern for the common man (aam aadmi). India ranks poorly in food consumption, fresh water consumption, literacy, nutrition levels, sanitation, education and low in primary healthcare and high in infant mortality and death during child birth. These need to be tackled by a combination of increased allocations; proper governance and devolution of powers.

Towards this, the AIADMK proposes the following : NREGS to be revamped and renamed as National Rural Upliftment Scheme - 75% of disbursals under NRUS to be in kind and the balance in cash. This will ensure family security
and prevent wasteful expenditure on liquor. PRIs will be involved in implementation of NRUS.
Ensure at least 150 days of work for those enrolled under

- Launch a Household Essentials Scheme linked to NRUS, which is designed to banish hunger from poor families. This will provide every worker, who works for five days in a month under the NRUS, a package of 25 kgs of rice or wheat, 1 kg pulses, 1 kg edible oil and 5 litres of kerosene to meet a family’s basic food requirements for a whole month.
A person who has registered 100 days of work under NRUS shall also be entitled to 2 dhothis and 2 sarees in a year.
Improve credit-deposit in rural India.
Transfer Rs 20,000 crores to Panchayats directly in consultation with the States to maintain local infrastructure, health and education.
Water bodies including estuaries to be deepened and repaired.
Aim for double digit manufacturing growth and 15% services sector growth.
Exclusive bank on the lines of Grameen Bank for small and petty traders.
Comprehensive rehabilitation package for all borrowers from banks suffering from global recession.
Use Defence Budget to leverage domestic employment especially with the Small and Medium Enterprises.
Expert committee to look into the efficacy of futures trading and implement necessary and immediate corrections.

Annadhaanam Scheme, on the lines of the scheme launched in Tamil -Nadu by the AIADMK Government headed by Ms. J Jayalalithaa, to banish hunger by providing food daily for all who want it through 10,000 places of worship nationwide. This number will be increased progressively.
Donations towards this scheme can be deposited in 7 nationalised banks. Such donations will be eligible for tax benefits.
Thrust on HDI - rather than on growth

Physical targets along with Budgets » Massive thrust on rural infrastructure & irrigation - Eliminate power shortages in the next five years — Thrust on conventional as well as non-conventional sources.
20,000 Kms of State Highways to be adopted by the Central Government.
Modernization of cities, including decongestion and building of elevated expressways.
Health, education and rural infrastructure spending to be hiked to 10% of GDP (Present : 6.5%). - All Central poverty alleviation schemes to be merged into a single scheme for better administration.
Target-based approach for improving literacy and education levels.
Retirement benefits for the un-organized sector.

A permanent Backward Castes Commission. - A package for traditional export clusters - promotion of brand India - Palm products to be encouraged for exports. - Women Self Help Groups to be re-vitalised. The scheme to be extended to men as well. ¢ NRI investment to be encouraged,
E-governance to be increased.

The biggest scourge confronting India today is terrorism. Despite repeated incidents of senseless terrorism targeting the hapless public, which have claimed several thousand innocent lives, the UPA Government singularly neglected to do anything to control it. Except for “stern
warnings” and vague assurances, the Central Government did precious little. Much time was wasted in the blame game.

Even while horrific terrorism continued unabated, the Indian Government took the unusual step of repealing POTA, overlooking the well-intended advice of political leaders from all over the country. While developed countries like the USA and UK enacted stringent anti-terrorism and anti-money laundering laws to tackle the problem of terrorism in their own countries, the Indian Government inexplicably chose to repeal even the existing law, thereby opening up the country's flanks to repeated terrorist attacks from inside the country and abroad. No wonder, since the Government rendered itself toothless to effectively tackle terrorism, and made the entire population vulnerable to terrorist attacks at any moment.

The AIADMK realises that the primary role of the Government is to protect its citizens. It recognises that every act of terrorism is an undeclared war on the Nation. Realising its constitutional obligations, societal aspirations and moral requirements, the AIADMK will work for the following: - A stringent anti-terrorism law with adequate safeguards to prevent misuse

A major problem India has been facing with regard to its neighbours is the porous Indo-Bangladesh border, which has encouraged the infiltration of Bangladeshi nationals into the North-Eastern region, particularly West Bengal and Assam. The UPA Government has not been able to complete the much expected border fencing and roads. As a result, infiltration by Bangladeshis has been continuing unabated and in such volumes that the infiltrators out-number the locals in many districts of several. States. This has understandably caused tremendous strain on the job market and resources in these areas, resulting in considerable tension and unrest. Even the electoral and religious dynamics in these areas have changed considerably.

The AIADMK undertakes to complete the border fencing between India and Bangladesh on a priority basis to ensure its completion within one year. Foreigners found to be overstaying in India or illegally enjoying the
hospitality of the Indian shores will be identified after proper enumeration, and will be deported honourably.
Commando units including Women Commando outfits to be established in every State.

Dialogue to be initiated and a special political package to be developed to address the genuine demands of Naxalites, provided they lay down arms. ¢ Defence budget to be increased to 3.5% of GDP against the present 2.5%.
The AIADMK will ensure that India's antiquated war machinery is modernised on a war footing.

The emoluments of Armed Service Personnel will be increased and their living conditions improved. Their concerns relating to anomalies in the wage structure arising out of the VI Pay Commission will be addressed and sorted out.
The long standing demand of Defence Personnel with regard to pay, retirement benefits and employment conditions will be favourably considered after appropriate consultations.

Retirement benefits and family security measures will be improved to such an extent that the Armed Services will become a favoured employment destination of the talented youth of this country. All the three Defence Services will be geared up to such an extent that they will be ready to take on anyone at any time.
A special package will be created to suitably rehabilitate the family of defence personnel who lay down their lives in the service of the Motherland.
All existing vacancies to be filled. New ones to be created.

Chip-embedded National Citizen Identity Cards to be issued to every Indian citizen. These cards will contain all relevant information about the holder and can be accessed on scanning by authorized officials of different Government bodies such as the Police, the Income Tax Department, Passport and Immigration authorities, Election Commission, Regional Transport authorities, State Revenue Departments, Banks, etc.

The embedded micro-chip/barcode will store data regarding the person's name, date of birth, address, credit details, vehicle details, criminal record, etc. For security purposes, the coding will be done in such a way that authorities of a particular department can access information that is relevant or necessary for that department only. 1 * The task of enumerating every individual and issuing such ID cards is huge. It will open up new vistas for employment in the Government, in addition to reviving the IT sector that has been virtually crippled in the wake of the global recession.

The AIADMK will also seek to solve the vexatious Ram Temple issue through negotiations and discussions involving all the parties concerned. If such an initiative fails -- the decision of the Apex Court on the matter shall be deemed final and respected.
The AIADMK will address the political as well as economic concerns of the North Eastern States & Minority communities.
Get to the roots of both economic terrorism and the economy of terrorism and put in place the necessary F safeguards to ensure that terrorism does not get funded internally or from abroad.

A tough line in relation to terrorism does not mean unfriendly international relations, especially with our neighbours. The AIADMK shall strive for an independent foreign policy. It shall not be a camp follower of any superpower as the UPA Government reduced this proud Nation into being.

The AIADMK will work for ironing out longstanding border disputes with neighbouring countries, without jeopardizing the Nation's security or integrity. Every effort will be taken to ensure that India's interests are not compromised or sacrificed in any way...

The AIADMK will work to ensure that pending border issues with China and Pakistan including Arunachal Pradesh and Kashmir are settled through bilateral talks. The whole of Kashmir will be treated as an integral part of India.

India will play a responsible role at the SAARC and ASEAN as well as at the global level in coordinating with various countries in resolving the global financial crisis. The AIADMK will strive for a permanent seat for India in the Security Council of the UN. At the same time, the AIADMK shall ensure that India has more than token representation at all international forums, especially in the IMF and World Bank.
The AIADMK’s international agenda:
The AIADMK will call for immediate cessation of war in Sri Lanka and demand an immediate stop to genocide against the civilian Tamil population.
Tamils should be accorded equal status with the Sinhala majority, with devolution of administrative power in the Tamil-dominated provinces of Sri Lanka.

If these moves fail, then the AIADMK will press for a . separate State of Eelam to ensure that Tamils in the Island live a life of dignity. - A grant of Rs 10,000 crores will be provided for the restoration and development of the Tamil areas of Sri Lanka and for the rehabilitation of displaced Tamils after the devolution is completed.

The UPA Government has disturbed the time-honoured convention of evolving a national consensus on foreign policy. Despite strong opposition both in Parliament and outside to the Indo-American Nuclear Deal, the UPA Government went ahead with it. The AIADMK calls for the scrapping of the deal provided there is a national consensus on the same. In the alternative the AIADMK shall work for renegotiating the Nuclear Deal to ensure that none of India’s long-term or short-term interests are compromised.
The AIADMK shall be committed to minimal nuclear deterrence. If need be, and based on the advice of the scientific community, the AIADMK shall keep the options of further nuclear testing open.

The gifting away of Kachchatheevu ‘to Sri Lanka by a former Congress Central Government headed by Smt. Indira Gandhi, courtesy Karunanidhi, under the Agreement of 26" June 1974, was not only flawed under Constitutional law, but also created myriad problems for Indian fishermen operating from the Rameswaram coast. As a result of the ceding of Kachchatheevu, India's territorial waters have shrunk. Our Tamil Fishermen, inadvertently crossing the international boundary, are being unnecessarily harassed by the Sri Lankan navy. Many have lost their lives in firing incidents while several hundreds have been arrested and taken away to languish in Sri Lankan jails. Several lakh rupees worth of fishing boats, nets and equipment have been lost. Both the UPA regime at the Centre and the minority DMK dispensation in Tamil Nadu, have remained insensitive and impervious to the plight of these hapless fishermen.

Secession of Katchatheevu was unconstitutional. In the Berubari case of 1960, the Supreme Court decided that an agreement involving the ceding of a part of the territory of India in favour of a foreign State can be effected only through an amendment to the Constitution of India which has to be ratified by Parliament. This has not been done in the case of Katchatheevu.

Further, in its agreement with Sri Lanka, the Union Government put the boundary line 1 nautical mile west of the Katchatheevu Island. As per Article 3 of the Constitution, any alteration of the boundary of the State . should have been first referred to the State Legislature concerned for expressing its views.

The DMK Government in power at that time under Karunanidhi, never took efforts to prevent the Kachchatheevu Island from being ceded unconstitutionally to Sri Lanka. Whereas in the transfer of Berubari, West Bengal’s then Congress Government went to the Supreme Court against the decision of the Nehru Government at the Centre.

The AIADMK General Secretary Ms. Jayalalithaa has already moved the Supreme Court to rescind the agreement with Sri Lanka relating to Kachchatheevu. The AIADMK Party will do everything necessary to retrieve Kachchatheevu from Sri Lanka and alleviate the problems of the fishing community in South India.

The record of the UPA Government in the Agriculture Sector has been abysmal. It had the mortification of witnessing large scale suicides by farmers across the country. Farmer suicides are primarily the by- products of a losing economy. A country of 1 billion plus people has to be self sufficient in agriculture. No country in the world has such surpluses as are needed to feed us, if we slip on our farm production even partially.

Subsidies that were available for farming were arbitrarily cut citing conditions allegedly imposed by the WTO treaty. This neglect has turned agriculture into a non-remunerative, financially unviable proposition. This in turn has driven the modern generation away from this vital field.
Further, those who were looking for big profits were lured into using genetically modified (GM) seeds, most of which are unsuitable for Indian conditions.

The AIADMK believes that increased food grains production, coupled with improved rural infrastructure, is the route to addressing India’s employment and agricultural crisis and improving HDI while concurrently addressing the challenges of economic recession.
To ensure an agricultural renaissance in India, the AIADMK plans the following: - All existing farm loans, including those’ with non-nationalized commercial banks to be waived.
Interest subvention scheme (loans at lower rates of interest) for food crops - including zero interest loans for critical crops. ¢ 30 Million Hectares to be brought under irrigation.
Water table in the country to be raised systematically through rain-water harvesting and proper chanellising of flood waters.
¢- Subsidy for seeds and fertilizers to be resumed. : No more promotion of Genetically Modified seeds.
Promote use of bio-fertilizers.

Perarignar Anna and Puratchi Thalaivar MGR did not, and Puratchi Thalaivi Jayalalithaa does not have any personal animosity to the Hindi language as such and the development and democratic rights of the Hindi ; speaking people in the country. India is a multi-lingual country with a long history of several developed rich languages and cultures and ethnic groups. ; Realising the danger that would be caused to the unity of India if there was any imposition of Hindi on non-Hindi speaking people, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru gave a solemn assurance in the Lok Sabha on August 7, 1959, while intervening in a debate on the language issue: "There must be no imposition. For an indefinite period -- I do not know how long -- I should have English as an associate additional language which can be used not because of facilities and all that, but because I do not wish the people of non-Hindi areas to feel that certain doors of advancement are closed to them. She also has the honour of having accorded the maternal role of women due legal recognition by legitimising the use of one's mother's name as one's initials instead of, or in addition to, the father's. Again, it was Ms Jayalalithaa who provided the impetus for the growth ofWomen Self-help

The Sethusamudram Shipping Channel Project was a dream project of the people of Tamil Nadu for over 150 years. The British first conceived the project but dropped it. Later, eminent personalities like Perarignar Anna and Puratchi Thalaivar MGR also felt that this scheme would meet a long-standing need of Tamil Nadu. It is this that the DMK and the UPA keep quoting to show that by implementing the project they are only fulfilling what Anna and Puratchi Thalaivar MGR had dreamt of. What is conveniently sidelined is the fact that the scheme is outdated in today’s era of high-speed, high-capacity ocean liners and cargo vessels.

By implementing the scheme, lakhs of fishermen living in the coastal districts of Tamil Nadu will be deprived of their livelihood, while precious marine flora and fauna unique to the region will be destroyed forever. Moreover, the scheme as it is envisaged today, involves blasting through Rama’s Bridge, a rocky ridge connecting India with Sri Lanka, believed to have been built for Lord Rama to cross over to Lanka. In short, the scheme in its present format does not assure any substantial economic benefits for the Nation. It will cause irretrievable damage to the environment throw lakhs of people out of employment and also hit at the faith of millions of people nationwide. The only beneficiaries of the project will be the Union Minister of Shipping, Mr T R Balu of the DMK and Karunanidhi’s family. The AIADMK will not back any scheme that is meant to benefit a single person or a single family, neglecting the larger good of the citizens of the country. The AIADMK will scrap the project.

In its stead the AIADMK shall bring about alternative freight corridors from Tuticorin in South Tamil Nadu to either Chennai or Bangalore. Also, the AIADMK shall ensure that Thoothukudi port is upgraded into a freight transit port.

Attempting to introduce a Common Entrance Examination for Medical Education which sounds the death knell for social justice;
Refusal to allocate power to Tamil Nadu from the Central Pool;
Refusal to give DAS Licence to the Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation, thereby denying the poor and downtrodden the opportunity to view a large number of channels at a low cost;
Continuous reduction in the allotment of Kerosene to Tamil Nadu;

DMK did not question the Congress Coalition Government and maintained silence when the Congress Government provided military training and supplied arms to the Sri Lankan Army for the annihilation of Sri Lankan Tamils;
Instead of taking steps to stop the genocide in Sri Lanka, the Government of India extended support to the Sri Lankan Army, which in turn killed a large number of Tamils;
DMK supported the anti-people policy of the Congress coalition Government at the Centre in permitting Foreign Direct Investment in Retail Trade;

Tamil Nadu, which was a power surplus State, was reduced to a power deficit State and the State was plunged into darkness; The acts of betrayal and the anti people actions of the DMK and Congress Coalition Government at the Centre are too innumerable to be listed here.
As the development of the States, including Tamil Nadu, is dependent on the Economic Policies, Foreign Policy and Fiscal Policy of the Government of India,

it is essential that a Government at the Centre is formed, of which the AIADMK will be an integral part, so as to restore the rights of Tamil Nadu, and to obtain for Tamil Nadu its due share, and for devolving additional powers upon the States. This is an imperative need
of the hour. Only then, will the rights of Tamil Nadu be realised and established.

Accordingly, the AIADMK pledges to the people of Tamil Nadu to fulfil the following promises which will remove the suffering and distress of the people of Tamil Nadu and will take Tamil Nadu to the Numero Uno position among the States in India.

Co-operative Federalism In the current scenario, the Central and State Governments should equally share amongst themselves Sovereign power and should not restrict each other and must act independently within their own sphere of jurisdiction.
They must find solutions by tackling common problems in a co- operative
manner. This is the principle of Co- operative Federalism. The AIADMK will take action to establish, enforce and sustain this principle.

Sri Lankan Tamils Issue The AIADMK is determined to ensure that punishment is given through the International Court of Justice to all those who committed war crimes and genocide against the Tamil minorities during the internal strife in Sri Lanka, which was against international regulations. The AIADMK is also determined to move the United Nations to take action and render justice to the Tamils in Sri Lanka and for holding a Referendum
amongst Tamils in Sri Lanka and displaced Sri Lankan Tamils across the world for formation of a separate Eelam.

Welfare of the Fishermen of Tamil Nadu Lakhs of fishermen in Tamil Nadu are dependent on fishing for their livelihood. The Fishing Industry occupies an important position in earning foreign exchange. However, fishermen of Tamil Nadu are being frequently arrested and tortured by the Sri Lankan Navy. On account of the swift action taken by the Hon’ble Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, release of the arrested Tamil Fishermen is being secured. However, the Government of India has not evinced any interest in finding a permanent

solution to this problem. On the other hand, it seems to be supportive of Sri Lanka. The AIADMK will take action to urge the Sri Lankan Government to put an end to the illegal arrest of innocent Tamil fishermen by the Sri Lankan Navy. It will also take necessary action to create a congenial atmosphere for talks between the fishermen of Sri Lanka and India, so as to protect the interests of the fishermen of Tamil Nadu.

Since deep sea fishing is a solution to the problem of fishermen, in order to encourage deep sea fishing, full grants will be given through the Government of India for the purchase of deep sea fishing boats.

In order to ensure the prosperity of fishermen in the coastal areas, the fishing harbours in Kasimedu, Cuddalore, Puducherry, Nagapattinam, Thanjavur, Pudukottai, Ramanathapuram, Kanyakumari and Thoothukudi will be modernized. River mouths from Pulicat to Kanyakumari will be desilted Sufficient funds will be allocated to prevent sea erosion in Ennore, Cuddalore, Poompuhar, Nagapattinam, Thoothukudi, Kanyakumari, Tirunelveli and Ramanathapuram areas.
For the welfare of the fishermen, the National Fishermen Saving cum Relief Scheme will be revamped.
Retrieval of Katcha Theevu The AIADMK is of the firm view that the retrieval of Katchatheevu is the only solution to permanently resolve the problems of the Tamil Nadu Fishermen.

The General Secretary of the AIADMK and Hon’ble Chief Minister Amma filed a case in 2008 in the Supreme Court of India, citing the Berubari case judgement in 1960 and praying that the ceding of Katchatheevu to Sri Lanka, which was part of India, by the 1974 and 1976 Indo-Sri Lankan agreements be declared null and void as it is against the Constitution of India since no Constitutional Amendment was carried out in Parliament. The case is still pending. In order to protect the interests of the fishermen of Tamil
Nadu, the AIADMK will take all necessary steps to retrieve Katchatheevu.

Foreign Direct Investment in Retail Trade The AIADMK has been incessantly opposing the policy of Foreign Direct Investment in Retail Trade and FDI in retail trade has not been permitted in Tamil Nadu. The policy of FDI in retail trade enormously affects the Manufacturing and Service Sectors in India. This policy will not only affect the livelihood of local small traders but will also annihilate unorganised retail trade. The AIADMK will take all necessary measures to rescind this policy at the All India level.
Tamil as Official Language Mahakavi Bharathi has glorified the rich tradition of Tamil language when he said, “There is no sweeter language than Tamil” and “action should be

taken to spread the nectar of Tamil across the world”. The Tamil language has a hoary tradition that is more than two thousand years old. Tamil stands independent of other languages. Tamil means beauty; Tamil means nectar; Tamil signifies youth. The long pending demand of the people of Tamil Nadu is to make this ancient Tamil language an official language of India. In order to fulfil this demand, the AIADMK will insist that all the languages included in the VIII Schedule of the Constitution of India be declared as official languages of India. Besides this, the AIADMK will take necessary steps for using Tamil in the proceedings of the High Court of Madras.

Universal Public Distribution System In Tamil Nadu, an Universal Public Distribution System is in vogue. Under this system, all the rice card holders are getting rice free of cost. Besides this, Palmolein is being supplied at Rs.25/- per litre, Toor Dal at Rs.30/- per K.G., Urad Dal at Rs.30/- per K.G. and Sugar at Rs.13.50 per K.G. This scheme guarantees total food security for the people of Tamil Nadu. On the contrary, the Food Security scheme recently introduced by the Central Government does not provide food security as being implemented now in Tamil Nadu through the Universal Public Distribution System. The AIADMK will take measures to replace the half-baked Food

Security Scheme of the Government of India with a Universal Public Distribution System, which will benefit all the people of the States, which are already implementing the Universal Public Distribution System.
Allotment of Kerosene The Central Government fixes the allocation of Kerosene to all the States.

The monthly requirement of Kerosene for Tamil Nadu is 65,140 KL, but the Government of India does not fulfil the entire requirement and has been continuously reducing the allocation of Kerosene over the past three years. At present, only 29,056 KL is being allocated to Tamil Nadu. This is less than half of the actual requirement. The
will take necessary action to get the entire requirement of 65,140 KL of Kerosene allocated to Tamil Nadu.

Establishing and Strengthening of Power Transmission Corridors Power Transmission Corridors are essential for purchasing power from other States, particularly the Northern States. As the New Power Transmission Corridors have not been established, and the existing corridors have not been strengthened, many difficulties have been experienced in transmitting power from surplus States to deficit States. Hence, the AIADMK will take steps for establishing new power corridors and strengthening the existing corridors so as to enable the transmission of
power from the surplus States to deficit States.

DAS Licence to Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation The Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation is providing cable services to enable the people of Tamil Nadu, to view a greater more number of channels at a lower cost. However, since the Government of India has not granted the DAS Licence to the Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation in Chennai, a situation has arisen in which people are forced to approach the private cable TV operators. The AIADMK will take action to obtain the DAS licence for the Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable TV Corporation. Likewise, at the All India Level, State
Governments will be encouraged and enabled to provide cable TV services.

Cauvery Management Board Although the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal was pronounced in February 2007, it was not published in the Central Government Gazette, because of the conspiracy of the then DMK Government and the Congress Government at the Centre. After Hon’ble Amma assumed office as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, she ensured the Notification of the Final Award in the Central Government Gazette dated 19.2.2013 after a protracted legal battle in the Supreme Court. The Government of India has not

yet come forward to establish the Cauvery Management Board for monitoring the release of Cauvery Water to Tamil Nadu by Karnataka, even though more than a year has elapsed since the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal has been published in the Government of India Gazette. A case pertaining to this is pending in the Supreme Court. The AIADMK will take necessary action for the expeditious establishment of the Cauvery Management Board.
Secularism India is a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic. Though India is a Nation of people speaking different languages, practising numerous religious
beliefs and following

multifarious cultures, yet we are united by the idea of one India, and of being Indians, first and foremost. Secularism means that all Indians have the freedom to practise their own religion and to pursue their own religious beliefs.

Though India is a land of diverse faiths, all Indians, irrespective of their religious denomination, share a mutual respect for each other’s religions. It is this belief in the idea of secularism that enables us all to live peacefully and harmoniously. It is the idea of secularism that enables us to look at all religions in a balanced and unbiased manner and to treat all religions as equal. The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) will strive to reinforce the idea and values of secularism in
Indian society.

Social Justice Social Justice, at its very core, means the creation of equal opportunities for all socially and economically weaker sections of Society. Our Social Justice Policy should aim at exterminating social inequalities and discrimination in Society. The implementation of such a policy will create a suitable environment for creating equal opportunities for all. It is based on such a foundation of social justice that Tamil Nadu has formulated and successfully implemented to this day, the policy of 69% reservation in education and employment. When the policy of 69% reservation was threatened by forces inimical to social justice, it was our Permanent General
Secretary of the AIADMK, our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi

Thalaivi Amma who gave the policy of 69% reservation the Constitutional shield of protection by getting the Act included in the IXth Schedule of the Constitution of India. The AIADMK will strive hard to continue to uphold the policy of 69% reservation.
Similarly, in accordance with the unique social structure prevailing in each State, action will be taken to implement reservation in other States.

Women’s Welfare Tamil Nadu is in the forefront of all States in formulating and implementing numerous schemes for the welfare of women. The Cradle Baby Scheme was introduced by our Revolutionary Leader Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu,

Puratchi Thalaivi Amma to rid Society of the scourge of female infanticide. This scheme is being successfully implemented to this day. As a measure of social security for women and to enable women from poor families to conduct their marriages without difficulty, a scheme of “Marriage Assistance” granting Rs.25,000/- and 4 grams of gold for Thirumangalyam, and Rs.50,000/- and 4 grams of gold for Thirumangalyam for graduate and diploma holders has been formulated by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma and is being successfully implemented in Tamil Nadu. Our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has introduced the Girl Child Protection Scheme under which, the only girl child in
a poor family is provided a grant of Rs.50,000/- as Fixed Deposit, for the benefit and welfare of the
girl child, and in the case of 2 girl children in a family, a sum of Rs.25,000/- for each girl child is provided as a Fixed Deposit.

Our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has also formulated several other schemes aimed at the empowerment and protection of women like the All Women Police Stations, All Women Commando Force, Women Self Help Groups, the revolutionary order enabling the Mother’s name to be used as an initial in the name of children, the 13 Point Programme -- a trail-blazing scheme for the entire Country for protection of women from sexual violence etc, are some among her innumerable schemes for the protection, development and welfare of women in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK will strive to
extend and implement such schemes for the protection and development of women throughout India.

Women’s Reservation “A nation that treats men and women as equals will surely shine as an enlightened nation,” sang the National Poet, Bharathiar. True to these inspirational lines of Poet Bharathiar our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, is firmly committed to ensuring equal rights for women in every sphere.

As a trail-blazer for the entire Nation in bringing about true empowerment of women and securing equal rights for women, it is our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, who brought about 33% reservation for women in the AIADMK Party organization
as early as in the year 1990. In the General Elections to the Tamil

Nadu Legislative Assembly in 1991, a record number of 31 women were elected. This historic achievement was due to the initiative taken by our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, to whom must go the entire credit. Our Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma is of the firm conviction that if women are to achieve real political empowerment, women’s Reservation must be implemented in State Legislatures and in Parliament.

The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has been consistently pressing this demand. The AIADMK will take necessary action to introduce and enact the Women’s Reservation Bill which will provide
33% reservation for women in State Legislatures and in Parliament.

Nationalisation and Interlinking of Rivers “From the surplus waters that flow through Bengal to the sea, let us sow the fields of the rest of India” was the fond dream of Mahakavi Subramania Bharathi.

The interlinking of the rivers Ganga, Tungabhadra, Krishna and Cauvery will bring prosperity to India and foster the spirit of national integration. Though 66 years have passed since India attained independence, no effective action has been taken for the interlinking of rivers.
Though there are many perennial rivers in the North of the Country, they do not benefit agriculture in the Southern States. While one part of the Country faces floods, storms and other natural
disasters, another part of the Country

faces the regular spectre of drought. If all of India is to be prosperous, we must enact legislation to enable the harmonious inter-basin transfer of surplus waters from one part of the Country to another for the overall benefit of all the States in the country.
The AIADMK will take necessary action for the nationalisation and interlinking of rivers.

Shareholding in Public Sector Enterprises As shares of Public Sector Enterprises are being divested to private hands, the Public Sector character of such enterprises is getting diluted. Public Sector Enterprises function with the goal of national development. If such enterprises go into the hands of private shareholders who only have a profit

motive, they will move away from the basic goal of national development. This will also cause labour unrest and labour problems will arise. Hence, the AIADMK continues to maintain its firm stand that PSU shares should not be sold to private entities. When the Congress led coalition Government at the Centre tried to divest the shares of Neyveli Lignite Corporation to private persons, not only did the Hon’ble Chief Minister, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma strongly oppose the move, but also came up with a very ingenious and unconventional solution of recommending the sale of shares to State Public Sector Undertakings in Tamil Nadu, thereby scoring a resounding victory. The AIADMK will ensure that there is no disinvestment of shares of Public
Sector Undertakings. The AIADMK will ensure that shares of
Public Sector Undertakings are not divested and will work towards completely stopping the process of privatization of Public Sector Undertakings.

Foreign Policy In the absence of strong leadership, India’s foreign policy has been weak and as a result, China has been intensifying its border transgressions; terrorists and militants have been active along the Line of Control in Kashmir with support from the Pakistan Army, and the Sri Lankan Navy has been committing excesses against Indian fishermen. The AIADMK’s firm stance is that to preserve the security and integrity of India, long standing border disputes with other countries

should be resolved. The AIADMK will work to secure a permanent seat for India in the United Nations Security Council. The Foreign policy of the Country should not hurt the interests of the States in the Country. Hence, the interests of the States will be kept in mind while formulating foreign policy.

Petrol, Diesel, Natural Gas Pricing Policy As the Oil Marketing Companies determine the domestic price of petrol and diesel based on the petrol and diesel prices in the international market and the US dollar-Indian rupee exchange rate, the prices of petroleum products are now being raised twice every month. Petrol and diesel are the key anchors of the Indian economy. As the Central

Marketing Companies continuously increase petrol and diesel prices, the prices of other essential commodities are also continuously spiralling upwards. 25 per cent of India’s total crude oil requirement is produced within the country. The balance 75 per cent crude oil is imported from other countries. When it is crude oil which is imported and processed in the country, it is completely unjust to determine the prices of domestic petrol and diesel based on international prices of petrol and diesel. If the price of petrol and diesel is determined based on the cost of production of crude oil within the country, the actual import price of imported crude oil, and the cost of refining the crude oil, then it would be
a fair pricing mechanism. This will ensure that the prices of essential commodities are kept under control.

The AIADMK will take steps to change the mechanism of determining the prices of petrol and diesel and will also withdraw the authority given to the Oil Marketing Companies to determine the prices of petrol and diesel. Action will be taken to determine the direct two- way exchange rate between the currency of different countries and the Indian rupee, i.e. a currency swap arrangement will be put in place. A separate Fund will be established to insulate and hedge the impact of variations of exchange rate on the price of petroleum products and thereby protect the common public
from adverse price shocks. Action will be taken to maintain the price of Petrol, Diesel and domestic LPG at the same level throughout

the year. Steps will be taken to increase the eligible number of subsidized LPG cylinders. The price of natural gas is being determined on the basis of the global market price and in US dollar terms. The price paid to developers and extractors of natural gas has been doubled by the Central Government with effect from 1.4.2014. This price increase will be reviewed.

Recovery of Black Money Indians have stashed away many lakh crores of rupees of black money from India in foreign banks. The Central Government has taken no action so far to recover such black money from foreign countries. When the AIADMK is part of the new Central Government
action will be taken to bring back to India many lakh crores of rupees which are lying in banks in foreign countries.

Review of Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements with Other Countries Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) are entered into between two countries to avoid taxing twice the income earned in one country and repatriated to another country.
The DTAAs are being misused to launder black money. Further, the DTAAs are also being misused to reduce tax realisation for India.
Further, the loopholes in the Transfer Pricing Policy are being exploited to evade tax. Action will be taken to enhance Indian tax revenue by eliminating
these loopholes and taking stringent action against those taking shelter under double taxation avoidance agreements to evade tax.

Vision 2023 The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has unveiled the Vision Tamil Nadu 2023 Document which aims at raising the living standards of the people of Tamil Nadu to the standards of developed countries, creating infrastructure to enable speedy industrial growth, and making Tamil Nadu the Numero Uno State in India. The AIADMK will take necessary action to prepare a similar Vision Document for the all round development of the whole of India as

Minorities Welfare The AIADMK shows the way for the rest of India in ensuring the welfare of the Minorities. The AIADMK Government in Tamil Nadu provides grants for Christians undertaking pilgrimages to Jerusalem. Every year 500 Christians receive such grants for undertaking the pilgrimage to Jerusalem. The AIADMK Government has not only increased the number of persons receiving the Ulema pension but has also increased the pension amount. The administrative grant for the Wakf Board has been increased to Rs 1 crore. A special grant of Rs 3 crore was provided in 2012-13 for the development of Wakf Institutions. To enable more members

minority communities to take up self- employment, larger loan assistance is being provided. The AIADMK will take necessary measures to ensure that these welfare measures are implemented throughout India.
The long pending demand to include Scheduled Caste converts to other religions in the list of Scheduled Castes will be fulfilled.

Welfare of Senior Citizens Respect for elders is an integral part of Indian culture. However, with the growth of nuclear families, the family based safety net that senior citizens could fall back upon is fraying. To overcome this situation, Tamil Nadu today provides Rs 1000 per month as social security
pension to nearly 37 lakh people including old aged persons in the State.
The AIADMK will take action to increase the old age pension amount paid by the Central Government.

It is essential to provide medical care for senior citizens. To address this need, the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Puratchi Thalaivi Amma has ensured that the coverage under the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Insurance Scheme is provided without any age restriction. The AIADMK will take action to implement such a Comprehensive Medical Insurance Scheme all over the Country.

Welfare of the Differently Abled The AIADMK is determined that differently abled persons should be enabled to live a life of dignity and independence. Maintenance allowance for differently abled persons has been raised to Rs 1500 per month in Tamil Nadu. Action will be taken to provide a similar maintenance allowance all over the country. Further, a special drive will be launched to fill up 3 per cent reservation provided for differently abled persons in Government. The benefit provided under Section 80 DD of the Income Tax Act for differently abled persons or their families will be increased to Rs 100,000 from the existing Rs
50,000. A time bound programme will be launched to ensure the accessibility of public buildings to differently abled persons by provision of ramps.

Amending the Income Tax Act to ensure that States are not deprived of Revenues Till 2012-13, various levies like privilege fee, vend fee, licence fees paid by State Public Sector Undertakings to the State Government were allowed to be deducted from the income of the PSUs for payment of tax. The Finance Bill 2013 amended Section 40 of the Income Tax Act to provide that any amount paid by way of fee, charge, etc. which is levied exclusively on a State Government Undertaking, by the State Government, shall not be allowed as
deduction for the purposes of computation of income of such undertakings. This
provision has hurt the non-tax revenues of the State considerably.
The Government of India will earn additional income tax in the process.
The provision also does not apply to Central Public Sector Undertakings.
The AIADMK will take necessary steps to withdraw this Amendment to the Income Tax Act.

Coal Scam The Central Government had taken a decision as early as in 2004 that the license to mine coal, which is very essential for power generation, would be allocated to private parties on the basis of open auctions. However, the Central Government did not create the framework for such auctions. Instead, coal mining licenses at different

locations were given to various private parties on a nomination basis. As a result, many private entities gained windfall profits. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India has reported that the Central Government suffered a loss of Rs 1,86,000 crores as a result of the award of coal mining licenses to private players. The AIADMK will take necessary action to modify the coal mining policy to ensure that State Public Enterprises are able to obtain coal at lower prices and at the same time the revenue to the Central Government is increased.
Ensuring Fair Pricing of Natural Resources The AIADMK is firmly of the view that the natural resources of the Country should be made available
consumers at a fair price. To enable this, a transparent Natural Resources Policy will be formulated by the AIADMK.

Personal Income Tax Currently, any person earning an income of more than Rs. 2 lakhs is required to pay income tax under the Income Tax Act. As a result the common people are adversely affected. At a time when they are battling inflation and price rise, the burden of income tax further oppresses the common people. To provide some relief to the common people, the AIADMK will take necessary action to increase the Income Tax exemption limit to Rs. 5 lakhs.

Foreign trade is important not only to earn foreign exchange, but also for the overall economic development of the Country. The trade policy should not only enable competitiveness, but should also ensure that there are opportunities for domestic enterprises to grow into large international entities. When there is no protection for domestic production and goods and the emphasis is on imports, domestic agricultural and industrial production is affected, resulting in people employed in such industries losing their jobs. The Central Government has permitted foreign investment even in retail trade. The AIADMK’s policy is that there should be adequate protection for domestic

industries; domestic industries should be made internationally competitive, and imports should be reduced, while exports are enhanced. The AIADMK is of the view that only through such a policy will it be possible to combat inflation and to control the depreciation of the Indian rupee.
The AIADMK will take necessary action to implement such a policy.

Action to Augment the Financial Resources of States There is no doubt that the State Governments are in much closer contact with the people. The responsibility for allocating funds for public services like education, public health, food security, nutrition and family welfare is vested with

the States. To provide such services, financial resources are very essential. To deliver the basic services that the people need, State Governments are in need of resources. However, the powers to raise resources are concentrated in the Central Government. The AIADMK is of the view that the mode of distribution of these financial resources to the States needs to be revamped. The Centre levies a number of cesses and surcharges which are not shareable with the States. They now amount to close to 8 percent of the Centre's Gross Tax Revenue. The AIADMK will insist that such cesses and surcharges should also be made shareable with the States.
The Central Government is releasing grants to States with
numerous conditions and administering

them in a non-transparent manner and at its own discretion. The AIADMK will take action to change this situation and ensure that grants are released to States in a transparent manner. The share of grants under Article 275, released at the discretion of the Central Government, in total devolution to States has increased to 18.1 percent of the total transfers in the Thirteenth Finance Commission’s period, up from just 7.2 percent in the Seventh Commission’s award. This is not a welcome trend as discretionary grants can be released on the basis of favouritism and in a non-transparent manner. The AIADMK will take action to limit the grants under Article 275
to 7 per cent of the total devolution and ensure that most of the resource transfer to the States takes place through the Finance Commission recommended tax devolution route.

The Central Government does not provide adequate resources to the States to meet their expenditure obligations and instead habitually tries to stealthily transfer more and more expenditure responsibilities to the States. The AIADMK is strongly opposed to this deceitful action of the Central Government. The AIADMK will take necessary action to ensure that if any subsidy burden is sought to be transferred to the States, then adequate financial resources are also transferred.

Opposition to the Recommendations of the Raghuram Rajan Committee The criteria evolved by the Raghuram Rajan Committee report to determine the level of development of a State are not the appropriate indicators.

If resource allocations to States are determined only on the basis of the Raghuram Rajan Committee report, it would cause a huge loss to a progressive State like Tamil Nadu and hence the AIADMK is strongly of the view that the Raghuram Rajan Committee Report should be totally rejected and will canvass this view before the 14th Finance Commission.
The AIADMK is very firm in its stand that, when grants are allocated to States on the basis of the resource gap,

the better performing States should be given adequate consideration, and further that, only the 1971 Census population should be the basis for determining the allocation of resources to States. The AIADMK is also of the firm view that the 14th Finance Commission should be allowed to make its recommendations independently without being influenced by the recommendations of the Raghuram Rajan Committee, particularly with reference to resource allocation based on the index of underdevelopment. The AIADMK will take necessary steps to ensure that measures to improve State finances are implemented.
Financial Transfers to Local Bodies The AIADMK will take necessary steps to ensure that 5 per cent of the shareable pool of Central Tax revenue is devolved to local bodies.

Macro Economic Policy and Financial Policy When a country’s imports exceed exports, it results in a trade deficit, which becomes the root cause of a Current Account Deficit. The difference between the foreign exchange flowing into a country and the foreign exchange flowing out of the country is the Current Account Deficit. It is necessary to promote domestic manufacturing and production so that it not only fulfils the domestic needs but can also be exported to other countries. Imports should be limited

only to those essential goods of which there is a shortage in the country. If such a policy is adopted, it will reduce the Current Account Deficit and enable faster economic development of the Country. The AIADMK will take necessary steps to adopt such a policy.

To ensure that the country’s economy is insulated from shocks, it is essential that the Indian Rupee’s value is maintained without volatile fluctuations. Necessary measures will be taken in this direction. The value of the Indian rupee is vulnerable to volatile fluctuations because of large volumes of short term capital inflows and outflows both in the
stock markets and debt markets.
Therefore, short term capital flows will not be
encouraged and only long term foreign direct investment will be given importance. Speculative trading in currency derivatives will also be eliminated.
Action will also be taken to bring down inflation. Consumer Prices inflation and food inflation will be specifically targeted and controlled by taking action to bring down input costs.
The Macro Economic Policy will be formulated in such a manner as to ensure higher growth, bring down consumer price inflation and reduce the Current Account Deficit.
Agriculture In 2011-12, food grain production in

Tamil Nadu reached a record level of 101.51 lakh metric tonnes. Tamil Nadu received the Central Government’s award for this achievement. Tamil Nadu has adopted many strategies for improving the production and productivity of agricultural crops like disseminating high-end technologies, popularising farm mechanization, creating irrigation facilities, developing post harvest and marketing infrastructure, creating storage facilities, and upgrading the capacity of the Agriculture Department. The AIADMK will take all necessary action to expand such initiatives all over India.
Action will be taken to waive the entire interest payable on crop loans for those farmers who repay
their loans on time.

The Congress led Central Government had agreed to a number of conditionalities targeted against Indian farmers in the World Trade Organization (WTO) meeting held in Bali, Indonesia, in December, 2013. Subsidies provided for Public Stockholding Programmes, i.e. for food security programmes were not deleted from the list of subsidies which are not permissible. The Clause which was agreed upon under which, if the subsidies exceed the limit of 10 per cent, they would not be challenged for a period of four years and would be open to scrutiny thereafter and the fact that the subsidies would be reckoned on the basis of the 1986 market prices are clauses which are against India’s interests.
Similarly, a condition has been imposed

that to promote trade the infrastructure in the ports needs to be improved. Such a clause only facilitates greater imports from developed countries. The AIADMK will take action to modify the clauses which are adverse to India’s interests.

Farmers’ Protection Programme The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had launched the “The Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Farmers Protection Programme” on 15.8.2005 with the aim of providing lifelong “womb to tomb” social security coverage to all agricultural labourers and small and marginal farmers in Tamil Nadu. In 2006, the DMK Government abandoned this scheme and instead brought in a new legislation. Since the welfare assistance available to farmers was not adequate

this legislation, in 2011 the Hon’ble Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivi Amma launched a new scheme “The Chief Minister’s Farmers’ Protection Scheme”. Under this Scheme, agricultural labourers, farmers and their family members are eligible for educational assistance, marriage assistance, maternity assistance, old age pension, and assistance in the event of death.
The AIADMK will implement the Farmers’ Protection Scheme, which provides substantial benefits to farmers and agricultural labourers, throughout India.
Manufacturing Sector The Manufacturing Sector is very important both for the overall economic

development of the Country and to provide employment. Tamil Nadu is taking a number of steps to develop the Manufacturing Sector. Many measures to promote both foreign and domestic industrial investment are being implemented in Tamil Nadu.
