The principle of the DMK is to create wholesome and genuine federalism with complete autonomy for States, amending the Constitution accordingly. On this basis, for the first time in India, the DMK has adopted State autonomy resolution in the State Assembly as early as 1974.

The DMK will continue to press for complete removal of Article 356 of the Constitution for the dismissal of elected State governments, not found in any other Federal systems and discrediting India, the biggest democracy in the world.

In view of the changing world economic, social and political situation, the DMK will continue to strive for adopting necessary Constitutional amendment for the States to function with full rights as per State autonomy principle.

Secularism in India is the only cementing force integrating the people of diverse religions and different faiths. The DMK always believes that every individual, as enshrined in the Preamble to the Constitution of India, has the right to follow and independently propagate the religion of his/her choice and to promote peace and harmony as reflected in Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution of India.
The DMK firmly opposes any amendment to the Indian Constitution for a uniform civil code that usurps the religious and human rights of minorities in India.
The DMK will not hesitate to prevent any harm to people belonging to any religion by those belonging to any other religion and stand firmly in protection ofthose affected.

The Dravidian Movement’ was formed to abolish caste-based discrimination and to implement reservation policy in order to ensure access to education and employment for weaker sections of the society according to their population proportionate to the total population.

In the National Front government led by Thiru. V.P.Singh, in which the DMK participated, it was decided to accept implementation of the recommendations of the Mandal Commission based on the resolution adopted in the Tamil Nadu Assembly during DMK rule. This was a landmark in the history of India. But, due to the judgement of the Supreme Court on Reservation, there is some interruption in the full implementation of the principle of social justice.

Reservation fixed at the maximum of 50 percent and the classification of "creamy layer’ as being not eligible for reservation are against social justice the DMK will press for amendments to change these restrictions.
The DMK will press for necessary Constitutional amendments to be brought to empower the National Backward Classes Commission on par with National SC/ST Commission.
Moreover, it will also urge for the creation of a separate Ministry in the Central Governmentfor the welfare ofOBCs.

The DMK will press for suitable Constitutional amendments so that the reservation policy in each state is left to be decided by the respective states in accordance withthe size of the BC, MBC, SC and ST population and insist to implement the respective states’ reservation rules in the offices of the Central government in the respective States.

Reservation is being implemented for SC/STs and OBCs in Central government jobs and educational institutions. But reservation is not followed in the Central higher educational and super speciality research institutions, which is against the principle of social justice.
Hence the DMK will press for suitable amendments to follow reservation in higher research institutions.

The DMK will not permit any change against social justice and reservation policies guaranteed in Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution. Moreover, providing reservation on the basis of “economic criteria” is not in keeping with Articles 15 and 16 of the constitution. Hence the DMK will continue to strongly oppose reservation based on economic criteria as opposed to the concept of social justice.
Efforts will be made for protecting and preserving the holistic welfare by delegating more powers to the National SC/ST and OBC Commissions.
The employment opportunities provided in public sector units is just one percent which is very low.

Moreover, in view of the public sector units being gradually privatised, reservation should be hereafter compulsorily followed in private sector too. Only that will be the just outcome ofsocial justice. It is to be noted that such affirmative action is in vogue in the USA also.
Hence, the DMK will continue to urge the Centre for compulsorily following reservation system in private sector also.

The Centre, which accepted Caste-based census, the long time demand of the SC and OBC people, after a debate in Parliament, has not so far released the findings of the caste based census. Moreover, the Centre announcing caste based census along with census for below poverty line people is contrary to the assurance given in Parliament. It should be noted that the norms for BPL are variable.
Hence, the DMK will urge the Centre to take caste based census hereafter, during the usual census count.

Although the Bill for providing 33 percent reservation for women in Parliament and State Assemblies was introduced in Parliament, so far it has not been debated and passed. The DMK will strive for getting this Bill passed.
The DMK will make efforts for proving free education up to college-level to women deserted by their husbands and girl children without support, depending upon their annual income.
The DMK will strive for formulating “a special health plan” for improving the nutritional status of SC/ST, OBC and BPL women.
The DMK will continue to urge for providing 30 percent reservation for women in Central government jobs as provided by Kalaignar during DMK rule in Tamil Nadu.
Statistics show increase in atrocities against women. The DMK will work for getting severe punishment for those indulging in such acts by expeditiously enforcing suitable laws for women's protection.
All sorts of child labour methods, should be banned. The DMK will urge for amendment of the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 1986.
The DMK will press for formulation of special policy and schemes regarding education, welfare, nutrition and freedom from violence and exploitation of children in the age groupof12-18.

The rights of children should be guaranteed by allocating sufficient financial, material an-d human resources. The DMK will urge the Centre to allocate 10 percent of budgetary provisions for the rights of children.

Besides creating a separate department for the physically handicapped, Tamil Nadu government led by Kalaignar, in recognition of their innate talents, designated them as ‘Differently Abled’. Further, it also formed a separate welfare board to provide them special concessions.

The Centre has already provided 3 percent reservation for differently abled in education and employment. But many government departments and PSUs do not properly follow this reservation. The DMK will press the Centre to strictly follow reservation for the differently abled.

The DMK will urge for protecting social justice by giving priority to SC/STs in the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court, to fulfil their just share.

We will urge the Centre for establishing a special section in Indian embassies for providing proper legal consultations to Indians going abroad for jobs and for solving the problems encountered by them.

The DMK will urge the Centre to appoint only Qualified Tamils as Envoys to the Nations in which Tamils live in considerable number.

The DMK will press for setting up this launching centre at Kulasekarapattinam in Tirunelveli district, which is very ideally suited scientifically and geographically and in the point of view of defence.

As expenditure in launching rockets will be considerably reduced in setting up launching centre in Kulasekarapattinam on the basis of the weight of the satellite launched and distance and expenses in taking to the launching site; and about 40,000 persons of southern Tamil Nadu will get direct and indirect employment opportunities, the DMK will strive for setting up the second rocket launching centre in Kulasekarapattinam.

The DMK will press the Centre for setting up the ‘Indian Space- Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre’ at Mahendragiri in Tirunelveli district. By establishing this centre, not only will the region itself develop but it will also be the basis for technological revolution in our country.

institute with capacity for courses relating to designing of aircrafts and helicopters, creation of ultra speed aircrafts and space technology researches, with the establishment of this centre opportunities will be created for the shaping of a lot of Students as Scientists from Tamil Nadu.

Moreover, the DMK will urge for providing basic and higher education to the children of Tamil families, prevent habitation of Sinhalese in Tamil areas and protect Tamil language, culture and places of worship of Tamils.

The D.M.K. will take steps to organise their resettlement after ascertaing their willingness under the Indian Citizenship Act and Allied Acts in consultation with the Government of India and make arrangements for their permanent stay in Tamil Nadu.

Seizing their catches and subjecting fishermen of Tamil Nadu to a lot of hardships has become quitecommon. Wewill press for finding a permanent solution to this issue continuing for several years now by the governments of two nations holding consultations with fishermen community and to form a Crisis Management Centre at the coastal areas of both countries for tackling this issue.
The DMK will press for changing the National Savings Scheme for fishermen in the equal ratio of 1:1:1 between fishermen, State and Central governments as it was earlier.

The DMK will urge the Centre to create a set up for establishing fishing ports in the coastal areas, to upgrade the existing fishing ports in Kanyakumari, Tuticorin, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Puducherry, Kasimedu (Chennai) with essential requirements like

water, electricity and fuel filling facility, to establish warehouses of international standards with modern air-conditioning _ facility in all fishing ports, to impart training in handling modern fishing tactics for fishermen to get due benefit for their labour and to make the occupation profitable, to distribute modern equipments required for it in subsidised prices and for teaching the methods of handling these equipments.
Further, the DMK will urge the Centre to start training institutes for fishermen to receive proper training for improving the storage of fish varieties for exports.
The DMK will strive for formation of a National Commission for Fishermen Welfare for protecting welfare of all sea and inland fishermen in India and take up necessary legal steps.

FISHERMEN IN THE LIST OF STs :- Fishing has been an occupation from time immemorial even before the advent of civilization. Traditionally fishermen are involved only in the occupation of fishing. Bearing this in mind, Kerala and Karnataka governments have included fishermen in the list of "Scheduled Tribes’. Hence, the DMK will strive for including fishermen all over India in the list of Scheduled Tribes and get them all the concessions available for STs.

Indian fishermen, particularly Tamil Nadu fishermen, are for long suffering from the atrocities like threatening, firing, seizure of vessels, cutting nets in deep sea, robbing the catches etc by Lankan naval forces.
The DMK will urge the Centre to create a separate Ministry at the Centre for protecting the interests of Tamil Nadu fishermen from the threats of other countries.

After Tsunami, people in coastal areas are living in constant fear of yet another high tide calamity. The DMK will press for passing ‘Coastal Community Natural Calamity Safety Act’ for forming a committee consisting of marine experts, researchers and engineers to take precautionary action to protect fishermen and people living along the coast.

Moreover, the DMK will insist for averting loss of fishermen lives by creating a Seamless Communication Network System for fishermen with Indian navy and Coast Guard and setting up helipads to save fishermen venturing on deep sea fishing.

Similarly, the DMK will press for removing the difficulties in obtaining death certificates by the families of fishermen dying in deep sea, and issue death certificates on the affidavits of fishermen organisations.

In many countries in the world the system of Sea Farming is being followed to breed sea creatures in select sea areas according to their nature. Fishermen with due training are involved in sea farming without affecting environment.
The DMK will urge the Centre to take suitable steps for following such sea farming system in Indian seas.
Tamil as Official language :- Besides undergoing numerous losses in opposing Hindi imposition and protection of our mother tongue Tamil, the DMK is determined to continue to work on that path.

The DMK has been continuously demanding to honour the assurance given by former Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru that Hindi will not be imposed on the non-Hindi speaking people as long as they desire it, and English will be continued as official language. In his address to the joint session of Parliament in 2004, the then President A.P.J. Abdul Kalam had said that study will be undertaken for making official languages of all states as official languages at the Centre. Still, the Centre has not made any effort to make all Indian languages as the official languages of the Union. The DMK will continue to urge the Centre to bring suitable amendment to Official Languages Act to make all official languages of all the States as official languages at the Centre.

On the basis of it, the DMK will continue to press the Centre for implementing the resolution adopted at the DMK conference in Tiruchi in 1996 for making Tamil language, the oldest in the Dravidian language family with rich literary and cultural heritage, as one of the official languages at the Centre.

Till then, it will also insist that the written tests and interviews for selection of candidates for all Union government jobs should be conducted in all official languages of the respective States apart from English and Hindi.

The DMK will urge the Centre to declare our mother tongue classical Tamil language as _ co-official language in Central government offices in Tamil Nadu, and the Central government offices, institutions and commercial banks should use Tamil for all their official purposes and for this suitable amendments should be brought in provision 343 of the Constitution.

We will strive for giving practical shape to the opinion expressed by legal experts for establishing in the four regions of the country four Regional Courts of Appeal and Supreme Court in New Delhi with the objective of devolution of the powers of Supreme Court of India.
As per section 7 of the 1963 Official Languages Act, it has been clearly stated “Hindi or the official languages of the States can be

used in the judgements and orders of the High Court”. The Official Languages Act stipulates that if a resolution is adopted in the Assembly for the use of this and sent to the President with the recommendation of the Governor, it must be accepted and order issued.

Accordingly, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Kalaignar moved and adopted a resolution in Tamil Nadu Assembly on 6.12.2006 for making Tamil as court language and with the recommendation of the Governor sent it to the Centre on 11.2.2007. But the Centre has not taken any decision so far. Hence, the DMK will urge the Centre to accept Tamil as court language of the Madras High Court.

The DMK, following the judgement delivered in the public interest litigation relating to River water nationalisation and linking in the Supreme Court in 2002, will strive for taking suitable action for nationalising all rivers in India kept in abeyance for long and linking of Ganga river in the North with Krishna, Pennar, Cauvery, Vaigai, Tamiraparani and Neyyar in South, for linking west flowing rivers in Kerala which are flowing waste in to the sea, forming an expert committee to give shape to these actions and finding out ways for implementing them, allocate plan expenditure for it, thereby increasing the full use of water available in India, through suitable water management and increasing productivity of Indian agriculture,
with a view to protect farmers and completely fulfill drinking water needs.

We will prevail upon the Centre for distributing power generated in States through Central power projects forthe sole use of respective States, supplying to other States only in the case of excess power generation, and creating grids linking all States in India so as to easily transmit excess power in one State to another power deficit State.

The DMK will urge the Centre to abolish death sentence following 150 Nations where Death Sentence has already been abolished in this twenty first century of advanced civilization and carry out suitable amendments to Indian Penal Code for the total abolition of death sentence.

Control of prices, rapid development in industrial and agricultural sectors, allocation of more funds for social sector, through which sufficient number of educational institutions all over the country, required hospitals, basic infrastructural facilities and employment opportunities for all, housing for all, increasing income of individuals and eradication of poverty should be the economic policy to be adopted inthe country.
Eradicating absolute poverty is more than a moral imperative; it is an attainable goal.

Only public sector units, as the basic infrastructure for economic development if India, were helpful for fulfilling the employment requirements of the people of respective areas. Special schemes should be formulated for profitable PSUs, forming the basis for social development and equitable economic development by creating employment opportunities for the sons of the soil, to continue to function and for strengthening and restructuring loss making PSUs.

Particularly we will insist that the PSUs in Tamil Nadu Hindustan Photo Films and IDPL should not at any cost be closed or privatised, and for their successful and continuous functioning proper investment should be made and technological know-how should be made use of. We will also urge the Centre to regularise contract workers in Central PSUs like Neyveli Lignite Corporation.

Further, the Centre has allocated Rs.8,000 crore for setting up another unit in fertilizer unit FACT in Kerala. At the same time, the demand for allocation of Rs.4,800 crore for expansion of Madras Fertilizer Ltd., in Chennai has not been heeded. The DMK will urge the Centre to allocate sufficient funds for the expansion of Madras Fertilizer Ltd. which has been functioning profitably for the past three years in succession.
During the last few years there is a trend of increasing inflation.

Similarly there is a crisis in repayment of external debts. The DMK believes that the basic reason for this is the increase in interference of non-governmental institutions in the policy decisions of the

government, and as a result the scare among investors. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to make appropriate efforts to control the interference of Non-governmental institutions in the policy decisions of the Centre.
60 percent of the total tax revenue of the Centre should be shared with the States.
The DMK will insist for the constitution of the Finance Commission and its terms of reference should be decided only in the Inter-State Council.
As Puducherry has for long been a Union Territory, we will continueto press our demand foraccording full Statehood for it.

In November 2011, the Centre permitted with some conditions, Foreign Direct Investment to the extent of 51 percent in Multi Brand Retail and 100 percent in Single Brand Retail in the Rs.50,000 crore retail trade in India, which has been the livelihood for 20 crore people.
But now the Centre has decided to relax these conditions and give various concessions for foreign investors.
Realising that a condition will be created in which several crore small traders depending for their means of livelihood and retail trade,
will be totally affected, if FDI firms plunge into retail trade utilizing these concessions, the DMK will strive for totally prohibiting FDI in retail trade.
The proposed Food Safety and Standard Bill to be introduced by the Centre has harsh rules affecting the occupation of small and micro traders in the lowest level.

Hence, though ensuring proper standards in food is essential, the DMK will urge the Centre to withdraw the legislation in its present form and formulate a new legislation in consultation with the small and micro traders.

Backward class and most backward class students of poor, downtrodden and middle class families availed educational loans from nationalised banks and completed their studies; many are continuing their studies. When such students completed their studies and are unable to get employment, the banks are pressurising their parents for repayment of such loans. Moreover details of students who had availed loans are put up on notice by banks, which mentally affect the students and their parents. The DMK will strive to change this inhuman attitude of the banks and waive the entire educational loans given to students.

The DMK will urge the Centre to establish in all district headquarters modern basic infrastructure in international standards required for providing training to the youth to attain suitable skill- level to participate in international events.
New Industrial Policy should be framed for increasing basic infrastructure for facilitating development of transport, electricity, link road facilities and water resources.

Generally the practice in governments working in the interests of the respective States demand and obtain required projects from the Centre and execute them. But it is condemnable that the ADMK government, in acrimony, has hampered the Chennai Port- Maduravoyal Elevated Expressway project, obtained from the Centre during DMK rule led by Kalaignar. Now the Madras High Court has intervened and ordered its execution. When works were started accordingly, the Tamil Nadu government has made an appeal in the Supreme Court against its execution. But the Supreme Court has not stayed. The works halted for several months have started again.
Hence, the DMK will urge the Centre to expeditiously execute and complete this project.

Kolachal is a natural port. With increasing world trade and full usage of Singapore and Colombo ports, multi-national ships are facing difficulties and loss without space for anchoring ships. To face increasing cargo ship transport Kolachal port has become very necessary. According to the study undertaken by the DMK government some years back, as the sea is deep enough for shipping near the port the Kolachal port can be developed into an international port without much expenditure. This port will serve as a Gateway for nations in the east and west.
Hence, we will press for taking necessary steps for developing Kolachal port as an international port with modern facilities.

The Employees Pension Scheme of the Centre is not beneficial to workers and many trade unions continue to agitate against this scheme. In this situation, the DMK will urge the Centre to hold talks with retired employees welfare associations once in three or five years and allowincrease in pension.

Similarly, the new Government Employees Pension Scheme is also not in the interest of employees. Hence the DMK will strive for reviewing this scheme by the Centre and for adopting suitable amendments so that there is no reduction in the benefits received prior to 2004.

The DMK will press the Centre to complete remove all ceilings on Bonus. The DMK will also urge for setting up a National Authority for Labour Welfare for monitoring implementation of workers welfare schemes.

About 2.5 lakh G.D.S workers employed in Postal department besides working for low wages are not considered as government employees or workers under Workers Welfare Acts. They are also unable to get all sorts of social security schemes like gratuity, pension and provident fund.
The DMK will urge the Centre to regularise their services and formulate and implement social security schemes for them.

During DMK rule welfare boards were formed for various types of Handy-craftsmen and unorganised workers including agricultural workers, tree climbers, barbers, construction workers, washermen, auto-taxi drivers, anda big scheme of providing relief fund of Rs.One lakh to the families on the sudden death of members of the boards, educational assistance to their children ranging from Rs.2000 to Rs 6000, assistance from Rs.50,000 to One lakh if one has lost his organs of the body during work etc., We will strive for extending such a useful scheme all over India. The DMK will press the Centre for creating a corpus fund for this and the Centre itself to bear all expenditure without fixing ceiling.

All Central trade unions in India including Labour Progressive Federation have been jointly agitating continuously during the past five years on 10-point demand. But even after many stirs there are no positive results causing disgust among workers. The DMK will continue to insist on the implementation ofthis 1-point demand.
The DMK will urge the Centre to start Employees Medical Insurance Hospitals in all districts and industrial towns.
The DMK will urge the Centre to increase statutory bonus paid to workers and government employees annually from 8.33 percent to 10 percent.
The Bipartite Wage Settlement for employees of nationalised banks anticipated since 2012 has not yet been signed.
The DMK will exert pressure on the Centre on this very important issue thereby urging early settlement.
The DMK will urge the Centre for giving Income Tax exemption up toa monthly income of Rs.50,000 (annual income Rs.6 lakh) for men and Rs. 60,000 (annual income Rs.7.20 lakh) for women.
The DMK will urge the Centre for giving Income Tax exemption for gratuity and provident fund paid on the day of retirement to retiring government employees.
If senior citizens have fixed deposits up to Rs.20 lakhs for five years the DMK will urge the Centre to give income tax exemption for the interest earned on the deposit.

The DMK will press for implementing a special programme on war-footing for creating massive employment opportunities for educated youth, by carrying out suitable changes in economic and industrial policies, and by establishing all over the country education and training centres required for preventing unemployed educated youth turning towards extremism and causing great danger to the society and country,.

Special efforts should be made for creating employment opportunities in urban areas. Besides creating new employment avenues in government sector, the DMK will urge for taking steps for creating self-employment opportunities, encouraging new industrial entrepreneurs, and encouraging those engaged in small and micro industries.
The DMK will urge for drafting a Small Industries Priority List for the educated youth to get employment opportunities, in small and rural industries.

Particularly, the DMK will press for industrial and service sectors like garment manufacturing, fruit juice, cool drinks, food processing, small home needs, handicraft goods, matches, distribution of cooking oil etc., to find place in this list.

At present, lakhs of Indians are working in various units in Gulf countries. But owing to policy changes adopted by those countries lakhs are losing jobs and returning to motherland. The DMK will urge for constitution of a committee to take decision by studying their problems and allocate required fund for their rehabilitation to protect and guarantee their future life, and implement the recommendations of the committee.
We will urge the Centre to provide monthly dole for youth who have completed school final and graduation and registered in employment exchanges waiting for employment, till they get suitable jobs.

Similar to the appointment of People's welfare workers during the DMK rule, under rural employment scheme for creating awareness among beneficiaries to understand government schemes to avail the benefits, we will press for appointment of ten lakh women who have studied up to 10" standard as women rural workers at all India level.

Simiarto the appointments during DMK rule led by Kalaignar for maintenance of State highways, we will press for appointment of 10 lakh youth who have studied up to 10" standard as road workers for maintaining roads with high standards laid under Central government projects, 13,000 km Golden Quadrilateral roads, and east-west; north- south national highways.
The DMK will endeavour for appointment of an expert committee to take up efforts for supplying potable drinking water to citizen all over the country and for regularising drinking water supply.

Madras city has been very much affected due to drinking water paucity. The same condition prevails in all rural and urban areas. The DMK will press the Centre for financial assistance as an emergency measure to alleviate this.

With ground water level fast depleting, taking into account water level used by industries operating in various parts of India, the DMK will urge the Centre to bring a new legislation for implementing rainwater harvesting projects compulsorily and for making profitable industries to use a percentage of their profits for these projects.

We will press for formulating and implementing special projects for generating non-conventional energy with the energy sources of air, sun light and sea waves so as to give priority to sustained growth and environmental protection.
The DMK will press the Centre to devise a plan and execute it for generating solar energy on government lands in villages considering the requirement of the respective villages.
Preventive Health Care: The DMK will press for extending to all India level the Preventive Health Care scheme “(Varumun Kaappom)” introduced during DMK rule and well received by the people.
Further, the DMK will urge the Centre to allocate 3 percent of Gross Domestic Product for public health schemes.

Crores of people in India are following natural medical systems in India like Siddha, Ayurveda, Homeopathy and Unani. The DMK will urge the Centre to establish ‘University for Siddha and Unani medical Systems’ in Tamil Nadu on the lines of Dr.Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan Ayurveda Medical University in Rajasthan for carrying out higher research in Indian medical systems.

Education was only in the State List as per the Constitution of India which came into force in 1950. The Kothari Commission (1966) appointed by the Government of India also recommended that the education should be kept in the State List in view of the — ethnic, cultural and linguistic diversities prevailing in India. After 1976, education was shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List. As it is realised by experience that several interferences and contradictions occur and the progress of education is retarded due to the existence of dual authorities, the DMK will insist for bringing education from the concurrent list to the State list again.
In the last 2004 Parliament election manifesto of the DMK, it was recommended that 6 percent of GDP should be allocated to education.
Still 6 percent of GDP is not yet allocated for education. With increase in number of those studying, the DMK will urge the Centre to allocate 7 percent of GDP for education.
We will insist that rules of electricity regulations be relaxed to give right to the States if State governments try to provide free power to agriculture.
We will strive for fixing minimum support price for agricultural produce like food grains, fruits, vegetables and invite views to find ways for increasing agricultural production.
We will undertake efforts for formulating proper plans for commercial production of food products, for processing and preserving them.

We will urge for distribution of full compensation calculating cultivation expenses of farmers when agricultural crops are affected by natural calamities like drought, cyclone and floods. For crop insurance scheme to fully benefit farmers, we will urge for holding consultations with farmers associations for simplifying the scheme to bring required changes.

By preventing the developed countries giving concessions to their farmers violating the rules of the WTO and affecting exports of agricultural products by developing countries, we will urge for taking action to protect farmers of our country.

The DMK will strive for paving way for all sugar mills - cooperative, public sector and private to make payment to sugarcane growers fully both support price fixed by the Centre and additional price paid by State government within three months of procuring sugarcane from the farmers.
In viewofthe difficulties undergone by tea growers, the DMK will urge the Centre to take all actions to alleviate them.

The DMK will press for evolving schemes for commercial production of vegetables, fruits and flowers and for increasing their export concessions. For this the DMK will urge for taking steps for establishing Regional Horticulture Board in Tamil Nadu and National Institute of Plant Biology at the national level.

The DMK will insist on establishing in every district sufficient number of warehouses, particularly air-conditioned warehouses for perishable items, for proper storage of food grains, vegetables, fruits and flowers produced in the country.

The Central government has made an agreement with a private firm for commercially extracting methane gas from under the ground in Cauvery delta region of Tiruvarur and Thanjavur districts. As it was said then that there will be no impact due to that project the Tamil Nadu government accepted the proposal in goodwill. But when methane gas wells were deeply bored besides the underground water level falling down very much and sea water entering and as that land will become uncultivable the farmers of that area are strongly opposing the project. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to give up the project for extracting methane gas in Cauvery delta region and protect agriculture.

As there is severe manpower shortage for harvesting paddy in the right time for farmers of Cauvery delta districts, the Centre should provide required paddy harvesting machines with 100 percent subsidy to every cooperative society in villages and the Society will collect a minimum rent from the farmers for maintaining the machines.

The DMK will urge the Centre to take suitable action for village cooperative society fixing and collecting minimum amount as rent from the farmers of that area for maintenance expenses of paddy harvesting machines.

Besides the fact that organic farming will keep the soil healthy and safe for long and the food crops produced by follwing this method will contain no poisonous ingredients. Hence the D.M.K. will take steps to implement ascheme for promoting organic farming, allocate sufficient funds and distribute inputs required for farmers using this method.

In view of the economic condition of small and marginal farmers who depend only upon their land and labour not being able to buy seeds, fertilizers, inputs and pesticides required for cultivation of their lands, the DMK will urge the Centre to provide them 100 percent subsidy for the above inputs to undertake cultivation.
The DMK will urge the Centre to waive all loans obtained by small farmers and the government should supply them seeds, fertilizers, inputs and pesticides as subsidy.

Considering the present price rise of inputs, fertilizers and pesticides and increase in agricultural wages required for paddy, sugarcane and coconut cultivated by most of the farmers in Tamil Nadu, the DMK will urge the Centre to increase the Minimum Support Price now and then according to the need of the respective states, particularly this year fixing the price of Sugarcane per ton - Rs. 3,500 Paddy per quintal - Rs. 2,500 Copra per Kg. - Rs. 90 and ensure the means of living of farmers.

Due to the price rise of inputs the cultivation of tea, being the means of livelihood of tribal people, is very much affected. Hence, we will urge for fixing the procurement price of Rs. 25 per kg. of green tea to protect thousands of tea farmers who are depending only on tea cultivation for their livelihood.

Besides taking legal action for keeping prices of consumer goods within control, we will take suitable action for controlling of essential commodities for benefiting poor and middle class families with less purchase power. As fixing prices of petroleum prices has been entrusted to oil producing companies, those companies with profit motive are raising the prices of petrol, diesel and cooking gas

every month. Due to the monthly increase, people are facing a lot of difficulties. Hence to avoid this, we will urge the Centre to change the price - policy for fixing just and reasonable price for petroleum products.

The DMK will urge the Centre to alleviate the sufferings of coconut growers by providing proper compensation for lakhs of coconut trees affected by pests and lost during the past ten years in Tamil Nadu.

Bearing in mind the scheme for giving free developed lands to poor farmers when Kalaignar was the Chief Minister, similarly the DMK will urge the Centre to bear one-time expenditure for developing uncultivable lands of small farmers into cultivable lands.

The DMK will urge the Centre to bring suitable changes in the Mahatma Gandhi Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme so as, To avert shortage of agricultural labourers required during agricultural seasons for farmers; To procure and distribute accessories like hoe and crowbar for those who working under this scheme and
To provide employment opportunities to all labourers in the rest of the year other than cultivation period.

The DMK will strive for devising a scheme to save salt producers from the circumstances in which they are affected by sea water rise and lose their means of livelihood and give due protection to them.

The job of saltern workers are not permanent and during monsoon season they continue to suffer without income. The DMK will urge the Centre to change this situation by creating a Commission for the welfare of saltern workers and protect them.

The DMK will urge the Centre for gauge conversion of all rail routes in Tamil Nadu; for removing level crossings in all highways and constructing subwaysorflyovers for unhindered road transport; as people living in all towns and villages are unable to use express trains, introducing rail-buses with two or three carriages from railway stations like Tiruchi, Madurai, Coimbatore and Villupuram to nearby places; laying broad gauge lines by providing required funds in the already announced new routes and bringing them to operation;
for taking suitable action for conversion of single line into double lines wherever it was not done in the broad gauge route between Chennai and Kanyakumari.

The Railway budget announced establishment of second unit in Chennai ICF Coach Factory. But so far this work has not started. The DMK will take suitable action for immediately starting the second unit.

At present the railway compartments are not hygienically maintained. Moreover drinking water facility and toilets are not sufficiently available in railway stations. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to take steps for undertaking cleaning work in railway stations, enabling differently abled and elders to use without difficulty and arranging proper protection to women in railway stations.

The Centre will be urged for laying the new railway route from TiruvanmiyurtoMamallapuram in the first phase and extending it upto Puducherry and for commencing study for Mass Rapid Transit System in corporation areas like Madurai, Coimbatore, Tiruchi, Salem, Tirunelveli, Tirupur, Erode, Tanjavur and Dindigul in Tamil Nadu.
The DMK will urge the Centre to attach in every train an exclusive compartment with 50 exclusive berths to enable differently abled to undertake train trips without any difficulty.

The DMK will urge the Centre to establish a “University of Railway Technology” in Tamil Nadu as in various countries for workers, engineers, train drivers, designers, technical experts and caterers connected with railways for getting higher technical education in various railway departments.

If the efficiency of Tiruchi Golden Rock workshop, situated in the Centre of Tamil Nadu with thousands of acres of vacant land, human resources and sufficient construction facilities, is fully used there will be no need for entering into agreement with private sector for a new Goods Carriage Factory.

If the railways execute this work, besides creation of new employment for thousands of workers in Tamil Nadu, this will become a milestone project in railways. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre for establishing new Goods Carriage Factory in Golden Rock.

The oldest Royapuram railway station in Chennai is unused now. On the basis of demand from DMK Members of Parliament placing the long time demand of people of Chennai city for developing Royapuram railway station into another Rail Terminus fund allocation was made in the 2012 railway budget for carrying out study for this. But
thereafter there was no progress. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to take up conversion of Royapuram railway station into new rail terminus without further delay.
The DMK will urge the Centre to bring the railway lines in Kanyakumari and Tirunelveli districts at present in Thiruvananthapuram railway division under the control of Madurai railway division.
The DMK will also urge the Centre to extend voluntary retirement scheme in vogue now only in certain departments to all railway workers.

The DMK will urge the Centre that just as the workers in Indian army and Para military forces are exempted from new pension scheme, railway workers who are working day and night for people of India also should be given exemption under the new pension scheme.

Airports in Tuticorin and Salem are without sufficient facility and without facilities for aircrafts arrival in nights. Tuticorin is one of the cities in southern Tamil Nadu with increasing industrial development.
Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to take suitable action for upgrading these two airports.

The DMK will strive for implementing the assurance given by Civil Aviation minister in Parliament for establishing Aviation University in Tamil Nadu particularly in Sriperumpudur for imparting higher technical education.

The DMK will urge the Centre to take suitable steps for implementing hovercraft project, which is a pollution-free transport facility, for increasing transport facilities in Tamil Nadu east coast areas; for creating jetties in Chennai, Mamallapuram, Puducherry, Pichavaram, Nagapattinam, Kodiakarai, Rameswaram, Tiruchendur, Kanyakumari and Kolachal for promoting tourism; and for setting up a separate Board for executing this project.
The DMK will press for further increase in the number of days for shipping between Chennai and Andaman.

With the experts telling that all the iron pillars of the more than 100 years old Pamban railway bridge have lost the full potential, there is need for constructing new bridge. Hence the DMK will urge the Centre to construct new bridge in Pamban area, and if Pre Stressed Concrete Beams and roofs are used for construction, there won't be erosion due to sea water and it will stand strong for long, and accordingly suitable plan should be undertaken.

The Keelanai bridge constructed across Coleroon river in Nagapattinam is much damaged. Repair works are undertaken now and then and temporary transport is carried out. Instead of this, taking into account the size of the vehicle transport at present and future the DMK will urge the National Highways Ministry to construct a new bridge.
The DMK will urge the Centre to implement Supreme Court judgement for increasing water level in Mullaiperiyar dam to 152 ft. as it was prior to 1977.

Though Cauvery river water sharing agreement between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka was legally extendable, following the Karnataka government adamantly sticking to the stand that it would lapse in 1974, the DMK government took various steps to protect the farmers of Tamil Nadu.

Besides adopting a resolution in Tamil Nadu Assembly in 1971 when Kalaignar was the Chief Minister, for setting up of a Tribunal for finding asolution for Cauvery River Water dispute; Following the resolution adopted in the Tamil Nadu Assembly in 1990 for the second time explaining urgent need for Cauvery

Tribunal, during the DMK rule led by Kalaignar, on 2.6.1990 when Thiru V.P.Singh was the Prime Minister, the Centre setup the Cauvery Tribunal. Accepting the demand of the DMK government for releasing the interim award of the Tribunal on 28.7.1990, the interim award was released by the Tribunal on 25.6.1991. The final award of the Tribunal was also released on 5.2.2007 during the DMK rule led by Kalaignar.

Though the final award has been released by the Cauvery Tribunal in 2007, so far the Cauvery delta farmers are unable to use Cauvery water to the required level for agriculture at the appropriate time. The DMK will press the Centre to setup immediately within a timeframe the Cauvery Management Board and Cauvery Regulation Committee to be formed according to the final award of the Cauvery Tribunal.

According to the agreement already entered into with Kerala, some more dams have to be constructed under Parambikulam-Aliyar project’, the lifeline of the farmers of Coimbatore, Tirupur and Erode district in Tamil Nadu. The important dam among them is the project for constructing a tunnel to bring water of Melneeraru river springing in Tamil Nadu to Tirumurthy dam.

If this project lying within Tamil Nadu is executed 4 lakh acres in the above mentioned districts will get good irrigation facility. But for creating hurdle to this project, Kerala government is delaying for the last 40 years without completing Idamalayaru project. If this project is
implemented, farmers of Coimbatore, Tirupur and Erode will get benefitted. Hence the DMK will strive for implementing this project with the financial assistance of the Centre and World Bank.

With global warming, the UNO and the Centre are pressing for giving preference to environment and extension and protection of forests. On the basis of this, for the first time in India, the Centre for Climate Change was established in Anna University during DMK rule for giving expert advice to the government by studying warming and seasonal changes. Many projects worth several thousand crore are executed by the Central and State governments and grants are also provided.
Considering the need for development projects, the DMK will insist that the environmental legislations should be drafted with “sustainable development”, as Objective.

The DMK will urge implementing a new scheme, with the assistance of the Centre, for the treatment of effluents from dying units, tanneries and washing units in Tirupur, Erode, Karur and Vellore areas and discharging them into the sea.

The personnel of Indian armed forces are prepared to sacrifice their lives for protecting our country. It is our duty to ensure the welfare of ex-service personnel who want to lead peaceful family life at
least after retirement after undergoing hardships during their service in pouringrainand severe cold, in forests and mountains.
There are about five lakh ex-servicemen living in Tamil Nadu.

An organisation called Tamil Nadu Ex-Servicemen Corporation is functioning in the State for their welfare. The committee headed by K.P.Singh Deo appointed by the Centre has recommended that only ex-servicemen should be appointed for administering this corporation. The DMK will strive for implementing this recommendation, one rank and one pension in letter and spirit, appointments of ex-servicemen in government departments and appointment of ex-servicemen for security jobs in government offices for the welfare and protection of means of livelihood of ex- servicemen.
All efforts will be made for the creation of Southern Gas Grid, which the D.M.K. has been pressing for the last forty years.
In particular, it will be urged to take suitable steps for bringing and distributing Liquified Natural Gas (LPG) imported in Dahej port in Gujarat to southern region.
Efforts will be taken for setting up a Permanent Exhibition-cum- Trade Centre in Tirupur, the hub of hosiery units.

Bearing in mind the cautionary words written by Arignar Anna, “Dangerous ideas in the minds of the jobless on the sides of roads; that's the sign of time”, the DMK will take efforts for formulation of a pioneer scheme to provide Shelter Houses for helping people without shelters sleeping on the roads.

We assure that the Candidates, who contest on behalf of the DMK alliance and get elected as Members of Parliament, will continue to strive for implementing schemes/projects incorporated in this election manifesto for the development and progress of Tamil Nadu.

People of Tamil Nadu, in practice, have realised, through the history of achievements accomplished by the DMK government, that as far as the DMK is concerned, the promise that 'We'll do what we have said; We'll say what we have done” was never made just as a word-adornment; through this manifesto, the DMK gives the assurance that we will do our Parliamentary duty and live upto the expectation and confidence reposed by the people on the DMK.
Therefore, we request that we may please be directed to work for you!
With the progressive slogans of, We'll establish secular good governance!
We'll preserve harmony among religions!
We'll protect social justice! Develop equality!
We'll strive for democracy to prosper!
We'll tirelessly work on the path of Anna!

Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) which was founded by our esteemed leader Perarignar Anna, on 17th September 19449, has, overa century old chequered history dating back to the dawn ofthe twentieth century. In fact, the seed of Dravidian Movement was sown way back in 1912, by Dr.C.Natesan. He started the Madras United League with the objective ofawakening the Dravidians from their long slumber and also set up the Dravidian Students’ Hostel in Chennai to provide facilities to students for stay for pursuing higher education.

Close on the heels, in 1916, Sir Pitty Thiyagarayar, Dr.T.M.Nair and Dr.C.Natesan joined hands together and formed the South Indian Liberal Federation which later came to be popularly known as Justice Party. The Justice Party echoed the voice of the non-Brahmins for reestablishing their social, cultural and political rights.

The clamour for Dravidian pride and rights grew more and more strident over the following years. As a result the Justice Party captured power in Madras Presidency and rendered justice through a slew of benevolent services benefitting the suppressed and oppressed people in the Presidency.

In 1925, the Dravidian upsurge witnessed another significant turning point with Thanthai Periyar launching the Self Respect Movement with rationalist ideals at its core. In 1938, Periyar became the President of Justice Party. The subsequent six years witnessed a renewed vigour of this movement in South making it to blossom into Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.

Responding to the need of the hour for a robust and democratic movement to meet the growing political aspirations of the people of Southern India and in particular, Tamil Nadu, Anna launched the DMK in the year 1949. Since then, for seven decades, the DMK as a responsible and vibrant political party, has been relentlessly and successfully working for safeguarding, nourishing and holding high the pride and honour of the Dravidian race, language, art, culture and civilisation.

After Anna, following his footsteps, the Party continued to play a crucial role since 1969 under the illustrious and unparalleled leadership of Kalaignar Karunanidhi not only at the State level but also at the national level to create a strong and vibrant economic system and to establish an egalitarian society, transcending the barriers of caste, creed and religion.

Today, under the able, dynamic and efficient leadership of the President of DMK, Thalapathy M.K.Stalin, the torch of Dravidian Renaissance is being carried forward with enthusiasm, unwavering confidence and deep dedication.
In this backdrop, paying our tearful and respectful homage to our sagacious mentors Arignar Anna and Kalaignar Karunanidhi who are
eternal rest on the shore ofthe Bay of Bengal after having created and led this great movement to spectacular success for seven decades we place this Manifesto before the electorate.

This manifesto reflects the ideal dreams and objectives voiced in the DMK’s earlier manifestoes penned by our late lamented leader Murasoli Maran, who rendered a distinguished performance as a Member of Parliament for 36 long years, and as Union Cabinet Minister for nearly a decade, under the able guidance of Dr.Kalaignar Karunanidhi.
While presenting this Manifesto 2019, DMK assures to provide honest governance and secular administration to the people.

The Indian National Congress’s secular and liberal nationalism has an equal place for each and every Indian. It is an inclusive vision. The BJP’s narrow and communal nationalism denies equality and equal rights to large sections of our people. It is an exclusionary doctrine.

The Indian National Congress practices the politics of consensus and cooperation The BJP practices the politics of divisiveness and discord. Instinctively, the Indian National Congress unites, while the BJP divides.

The tireless campaign of Smt. Sonia Gandhi, President of the Indian National Congress resulted in its return to the 14th Lok Sabha as the single largest party after eight years in the Opposition. She took the initiative to give shape to the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) comprising of the Indian National Congress, its pre-poll allies and supporting like-minded parties. The May 2004 mandate was for a government that would be responsive to the concerns of the aam admi and to the needs of the poor, the deprived and the disadvantaged.
This has been achieved in very substantial measure.
The May 2004 mandate was for a government that would accelerate economic growth but with a focus always on livelihoods and jobs, on inclusive growth and on social justice.
The May 2004 mandate was for a government that would take forward the agenda of empowerment of the weaker sections of society in a forthright manner with emphasis on education.
This has been achieved in substantial measure. The May 2004 mandate was for a government that would bridge all divides, that would bring all sections of society together, and give them voice.
This has been achieved in substantial measure.

The accomplishments of the Congress-led UPA government since May 2004 have been tangible and visible. The manifesto of the Indian National Congress for the 2004 Lok Sabha elections provided the foundation for the National Common Minimum Programme that formed the basis of governance during the past five years. It has restored secular and Constitutional values in governance. It has also made administration markedly more transparent. The Right to Information Act, 2005 is a historic legislation. Not only has livelihood security been provided to many lakh poor rural families but durable community assets have also been created.

It has started and achieved considerable progress on the ambitious Bharat Nirman programme to transform rural India by expanding and providing irrigation, all-weather roads, houses for the poor, drinking water, electricity for all poor families and phone connectivity in all villages.

It has brought comfort and hope to crores of our farmers and their families by (i) increasing the MSP and procurement prices; (ii) by waiving loans to the tune of Rs 65,000 crore; (iii) by increasing threefold credit from banks and reducing interest rates on crop loans; and (iv) by extending irrigation facilities.

It has launched the National Rural Health Mission which has already made a positive impact by improving the quality and accessibility of primary health care in villages. More children are now being delivered under the care of trained health professionals. Around six and a half lakh women have been trained and posted as accredited social health activists (ASHAs).

It has significantly empowered the weaker sections of society by (i) giving scheduled tribes and traditional forest dwellers rights over land they cultivate in forest areas; (ii) by providing reservations for OBC students in all professional institutions; (iii) by passing a new law to protect women from domestic violence; (iv) by giving women equal rights to inherit property; and (v) by enhancing hugely the scholarships for scheduled castes, scheduled tribes, minorities and OBCs to pursue college and university education.

The investment in higher education in the XIth Five Year Plan (2007-08 to 2011-12) will witness a huge increase – five times the investment in the previous five years.

This economic growth has enabled the introduction of the Aam Admi Bima Yojana (life insurance cover) for one and a half crore landless households, the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (medical insurance cover) for six crore unorganized sector workers living below the poverty line and the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension scheme for elder citizens over 65 years of age and living below the poverty line.
